title: MatchLens by Dhisana
tagline: When a goal is corrected, the AI story should change too. Four agents turn synthetic football events into reviewed, evidence-linked explanations for fans and analysts in English and Spanish.
description:
**Target category: Best Multi-Agent System (Best Multi-Agent Orchestration).**

## The story changes when the evidence changes

MatchLens by Dhisana AI, Inc., represented by Madhukar Devaraju, keeps football explanations in step with corrected evidence. A reported goal can be voided while an AI story and translated summaries remain confidently wrong. MatchLens updates the score, retracts the superseded citation and requires every localized story to disclose the correction.

Live demo: https://matchlens-dev.redforest-787f42f7.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io

Demo video (1:53): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qdtIEEIp8bE

Public source: https://github.com/madhukard/matchlens

## Purposeful multi-agent collaboration

Four specialists use the OpenAI Agents SDK and shared, versioned evidence. The match analyst selects the story and view; an evidence critic challenges its interpretation; an audience editor writes for fans and analysts in English and Spanish; a broadcast verifier checks all four variants. Feedback permits one correction attempt. Continued failure withholds the narrative and shows current statistics. Deterministic code handles score arithmetic.

## Azure architecture

An Azure Container Apps job uses managed identity to call Azure OpenAI and publish a private Azure Blob Storage ledger with facts, handoffs, review failures, latency and usage. A separate Container App serves the browser UI and read-only MCP tools with no inference role. Azure Container Registry stores the image. A storage lease, call/token budgets and timeouts bound generation. Public viewing cannot start paid generation. Resources are isolated from Dhisana production.

## Evidence and tradeoffs

Across eight authored synthetic cases, the multi-agent workflow passed publication checks in 8/8 cases versus 3/8 for a single-agent baseline. Mean generation time was 23.77 seconds versus 12.56 seconds. This small, unequal-compute comparison is diagnostic, not proof of general superiority; advisory grading uses the same model family. Outputs and failures are retained. The video shows the earlier four-case evaluation.

The live six-frame recording passes checks across 24 audience/language variants. Review caught a Spanish draft confusing pass attempts with completions and withheld publication, exposing a feedback-handling defect that was fixed and regression tested.

## Judge walkthrough

Open the free browser demo. Select Moment 5 (Goal reported), then Moment 6 (Goal corrected): 1–0 becomes 0–0. Open Show me why to inspect finish-4@2, the voided goal. Switch audience and language while retaining the evidence. No login or model key is required.

All teams and events are fictional. The six accelerated batches are a reviewed recording, not a licensed live feed. The correction reason is unknown. Counts do not establish tactical causality.

Claude Code live MCP acceptance passed. Connected ChatGPT MCP tools returned both frames; full visual interaction acceptance remains unverified. Copilot CLI was blocked by organization policy. The standalone browser is the primary judged experience.

See docs/judge-guide.md and docs/evaluation.md in the repository for walkthrough and reproducible evaluation.

title: Matchlens Studio
tagline: One match feed, a different broadcast for every viewer
description:
MatchLens Studio

One match feed, a different broadcast for every viewer.

The problem

A football broadcast tells one story to everyone. The analyst wants pressing intensity and expected goals. The casual fan wants to know why the crowd just got loud. A supporter abroad wants it in their own language, about their own club. Today’s on-screen graphics mostly report what happened, not why it matters, and they are the same for every viewer.

What it does

MatchLens Studio ingests synthetic, football-realistic match events as they happen: passes, shots, tackles, pressure events and possession changes. It turns them into explainable match intelligence that sits on screen next to the match.

Detects the moments that matter: goals, big chances, pressing shifts, momentum swings, the game tipping from control into chaos, line-breaking passes, player milestones, and speed and distance alerts.
Explains why each one matters: every moment carries the numbers behind it and reason codes, such as “the press is paying off”, “against the run of play”, or “the substitute changed it”.
Personalizes the same intelligence by audience (analyst or fan), language, favourite club, favourite player, a follow-player mode, and the metric a viewer cares about.
Renders timed, machine-readable overlay cues (lower thirds, stat cards, player tags, half-time and full-time recaps) that a graphics engine can sync to a live feed.

In the sample match, the same pressing shift at 63' reaches two viewers differently:

Analyst (English): “Calderwick are pressing 70% of Northbridge’s actions on the ball, up from 33%. PPDA has dropped from 9.6 to 7.”

Calderwick fan (Spanish): “¡Calderwick va a por el partido! Han dejado de esperar y salen a buscar el balón.”

Four minutes later, the equaliser is explained by that same press.

How it works

A five-stage pipeline:

Ingest: validate and order the event stream.
Interpret: running team and player statistics, pass difficulty, press rate, PPDA, threat share and a chaos index over rolling windows.
Explain: 11 detectors produce evidence-backed insights.
Personalize: each insight is re-scored and paced per viewer, with a record of why it was shown.
Render: timed overlay cues validated against a published JSON schema, streamed live over Server-Sent Events and exportable as JSON or WebVTT.
Agentic design (Microsoft Agent Framework)

The deterministic core decides what happened and why it matters. A multi-agent workflow decides how to say it to each viewer:

Tactical analyst agent: calls read-only match tools (team stats over a window, a player’s match so far, earlier key moments) and writes a short brief.
Studio writer and fan commentator agents: turn that one brief into copy for every audience, language and supporter stance watching, in parallel.
Fact checker: a deterministic gate, not a model. It rejects any draft that quotes a number the pipeline or a tool did not compute, runs too long, or uses analyst jargon in fan copy. A rejected draft goes back to its writer once, with the reasons.
Recovery: model errors, timeouts and twice-rejected drafts fall back to deterministic template copy. Narration runs in the background, so the match clock never waits for a model.
Ask-the-match agent: answers viewer questions through the same tools. A critic pass sends an answer back once if it quotes a number no tool returned.

The viewer shows the full trace under “Why this is on screen”: the analyst’s brief, the tools it called, and the fact checker’s verdict.

Synthetic data with ground truth

A seeded simulator generates realistic matches (about 2,600 events each) with fictional clubs and players. Each team follows a hidden tactic script, saved separately and never read by the pipeline. That lets the detectors be scored, not just demonstrated. Across 30 test matches, the scripted pressing switch was detected in 23, with a median delay of 5 minutes, and there were only 4 false alarms across 30 matches with no tactical change.

Built with
Microsoft Agent Framework: agents, tools and the workflow graph.
Microsoft Foundry models, through the Agent Framework Foundry client with Microsoft Entra ID authentication. [Delete this line if the live check hasn’t run.]
Azure Container Apps for hosting. [Delete this line if not deployed.]
Python, FastAPI, Server-Sent Events, and a browser viewer.
Quality
79 automated tests, run without network access. They drive the real Agent Framework workflow with a scripted model.
A published overlay JSON schema, which every generated cue is validated against.
A detector evaluation script you can rerun against ground truth.
Runs end to end without any cloud account, using built-in English and Spanish templates. Connecting a Foundry model enables the agent desk, more languages and the Ask box.
What’s next
Event Hubs ingest for live production feeds.
More template languages.
Scoring the momentum and rhythm detectors against ground truth.

All clubs, players and events are fictional and synthetic. No real league data is used.

title: MatchLens — Match Intelligence & Player Performance
tagline: Understand the match. Follow the players who shape it and support who did not perform.
description:
**MatchLens** is an AI-powered football experience combining live match intelligence with detailed player analysis. Built for the Microsoft × Premier League hackathon, it transforms synthetic, football-realistic events into clear statistics, visual insights, and personalized narratives for fans, analysts, and broadcast audiences.

At the match level, MatchLens identifies turning points such as increased defensive pressure, dangerous counterattacks, and changes in territorial control. It explains why these moments matter, supported by the events and statistics behind each insight.

At the player level, users can select any player currently on the pitch through an interactive lineup or pitch view. Each player’s dashboard updates as the simulated match progresses and includes:

- Playing area: Position map, touch locations, and movement heatmap generated from synthetic tracking data.

- Passing performance: Successful and unsuccessful passes, completion percentage, pass locations, and progressive passes.

- Playing time: Minutes played, starting or substitute status, and substitution times. Players who leave the pitch remain available for performance review.

- Attacking contribution: Goals, assists, shots, and involvement in attacking sequences.

- Defensive contribution: Tackles, interceptions, recoveries, and recorded pressure events.

- Physical activity: Distance covered and speed indicators where supported by the synthetic tracking data.

- Performance explanation: Short, evidence-backed narratives connecting the player’s actions to the wider match.

For example, instead of only showing that a midfielder completed several passes, MatchLens could explain: “Three of Santos’s passes moved the ball into the attacking third, helping Blue FC advance during this period.”

Users can switch between a simple fan experience and a detailed analyst experience, choose a favorite team or player, and select their preferred language. Live insight cards and automatic halftime and full-time recaps reflect those preferences while preserving the same underlying facts.

The project’s core pipeline is ingest → interpret → explain → visualize → personalize. All match events, player identities, and tracking data used in the demonstration will be synthetic. Statistics will be calculated from that data, with AI generating explanations grounded in the calculated results.

title: MatchLens: Explainable, Personalised Match Intelligence for Live Football
tagline: A multi-agent engine on Azure that turns live football events into explainable insights, broadcast-ready overlays and automated recaps. It explains why each moment matters, checks every number, and tells the story differently for analysts, casual fans and player-focused viewers, in their language.
description:
## The problem
A scoreline tells you what happened, not why. Broadcasters and streaming platforms have more event data than ever, but turning it into on-screen stories in real time still takes a room full of people, and every viewer gets the same graphics whether they analyse tactics for a living or are watching their first match.

## What MatchLens does
One pipeline, five stages:

1. **Ingest:** synthetic match events (passes, shots, tackles, pressure, possession changes, sprints, match metadata) stream in as they happen.
2. **Interpret:** a deterministic stats engine keeps live match state: pass distance, accuracy and a 0–10 pass difficulty rating, ball and shot speed, xG, possession, field tilt, PPDA, momentum and a control-vs-chaos index.
3. **Explain:** a moment detector scores every event for significance, and AI agents explain why it matters: a momentum swing, a pressure spell, a change in the game's rhythm. Every claim carries the numbers behind it.
4. **Render:** insights become timed, machine-readable overlay cues (start time, duration, screen region, priority) with a published JSON Schema, ready for a graphics partner to draw over the live feed. A web overlay demo shows them on a pitch view.
5. **Personalise:** the same insight is rewritten for each viewer: Analyst mode, Casual mode, Player Focus mode, favourite club, and the viewer's language.

## How it works
- **Two speeds.** Rule-based overlays (player name tags, speed and distance triggers, pass difficulty) go out in under a second. Agent-written narrative follows a few seconds later. If an agent is slow or fails, a templated caption is shown instead, so the screen never waits on a model.
- **Specialised agents with shared match state**, orchestrated with Microsoft Agent Framework:
  - *Analyst agent:* explains why a moment matters, using live match state
  - *Fact-checker agent:* rejects any narrative whose numbers don't match the stats engine
  - *Persona agent:* adapts tone, depth and language for each viewer mode
  - *Recap agent:* writes half-time and full-time recaps and player-of-the-match notes
- **Explainable by design.** Every insight links back to the computed facts that support it.

## Synthetic data
MatchLens ships with its own match simulator built around fictional clubs and players: a possession-chain model driven by player attributes, team style, pressing and pitch geometry. Averaged over 30 simulated matches, 14 box-score metrics fall inside typical top-flight ranges (about 1.75 goals, 14 shots and 430 passes per team at 79% pass accuracy, with the hardest-working players covering around 12 km). The same seed always replays the same match, so demos are reproducible.

## Built with
Microsoft Foundry · Microsoft Agent Framework · Azure Event Hubs · Azure Container Apps · Azure Cosmos DB · Azure Web PubSub · Azure AI Speech · Application Insights · Python (FastAPI) · React

## Roadmap
Auto-eventing from a video feed (a vision model generating pass and speed metrics), more languages and voice commentary, and a fantasy-manager mode.

description:
# MatchMind AI — Explainable Football Match Intelligence

## Overview

MatchMind AI transforms synthetic football match-event data into explainable turning-point insights, evidence-backed analysis, and engaging match recaps. Instead of simply reporting what happened during a match, it helps fans and analysts understand **why key moments mattered and how they shaped the story of the game**.

## Problem

Football match-event data contains valuable insights, but raw events can be difficult to interpret. Conventional summaries often describe goals and major incidents without clearly explaining their significance or connecting conclusions to supporting evidence.

## Solution

MatchMind AI combines deterministic football-event analysis with an AI-assisted explanation pipeline. Its analysis engine identifies significant match moments, ranks turning points, and connects insights to underlying event records. The platform then presents these findings through accessible narratives designed for fans and more detailed analysis for analysts.

## Key Features

- **Match Event Analysis:** Loads synthetic football-event CSV data and organizes it into a structured match timeline.
- **Turning-Point Detection:** Uses a Java-based analysis engine to identify and rank significant moments using event-based scoring.
- **Evidence-Backed Explanations:** Connects insights to supporting match events so users can inspect the evidence behind the analysis.
- **Match Recaps:** Transforms structured findings into readable, data-grounded match narratives, with a deterministic demo mode when live AI generation is unavailable.
- **Interactive Dashboard:** Provides a React and TypeScript interface with match summaries, timelines, key insights, and distinct Fan and Analyst views.
- **Synthetic Replay Experience:** Presents key moments through synchronized, broadcast-style replay overlays based on the available event sequence.

## Technology

**Backend:** Java 17, Spring Boot, REST APIs  
**Frontend:** React, TypeScript, Vite  
**Data:** Synthetic football match-event dataset  
**AI:** AI integration path with deterministic DEMO fallback

## Goal and Impact

MatchMind AI demonstrates how explainable AI can make football analytics more accessible, transparent, and engaging. By combining structured event analysis with evidence-grounded narratives, it aims to help fans understand the decisive moments behind a match and give analysts a clearer way to explore the story hidden in match data.

description:
MatchMind AI
Explainable, Real-Time Football Intelligence for Every Fan

Project Overview

Football is more than goals, scores, and possession statistics. Every match contains tactical shifts, turning points, individual performances, and hidden patterns that can be difficult for viewers to recognize in real time.

MatchMind AI aims to transform synthetic football match events into meaningful, explainable, and personalized match intelligence using AI agents and Microsoft technologies.

Our vision is to build an intelligent football companion that goes beyond describing what happens on the pitch. It should explain **why a moment matters, what evidence supports that interpretation, and how the insight can be presented differently to each viewer**.

We are currently forming a team and developing the project concept for the Microsoft Premier League Hackathon. We welcome collaborators interested in AI, software engineering, cloud computing, football analytics, and user experience design.

The Problem

Traditional football statistics often provide numbers without context, while automated commentary can produce fluent narratives without clearly showing the evidence behind its conclusions.

Broadcasters, analysts, and casual fans also have different information needs. An analyst may want detailed tactical patterns and performance metrics, whereas a casual supporter may prefer concise explanations, memorable moments, and updates about their favorite players.

We aim to address these challenges through a unified, evidence-grounded football intelligence platform.

Proposed Solution

Our proposed system will combine five capabilities:

1. Real-Time Event Processing

Ingest synthetic, football-realistic match events such as passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, and pressure events. Maintain a continuously updated match state and derive relevant statistics.

2. Intelligent Match Analysis

Identify key moments, changes in momentum, passing patterns, tactical pressure, and emerging player-performance trends using structured event data.

3. Evidence-Grounded AI Explanations

Use coordinated AI agents to transform statistical findings into contextual explanations. Important claims will be linked to supporting events and metrics to improve transparency and reduce unsupported AI-generated statements.

4. Automated Match Storytelling

Generate concise live commentary, turning-point summaries, player insights, and post-match recaps. Produce structured outputs suitable for synchronized dashboards and broadcast-style graphical overlays.

5. Personalized Fan Experiences

Support different viewing modes, such as Casual Fan and Tactical Analyst, with potential customization by preferred team, player, metric, and language.

Multi-Agent Architecture

We plan to explore a coordinated agent-based architecture with specialized responsibilities:

- Statistics Agent: Processes event streams and computes match statistics.
- Tactical Analysis Agent: Detects meaningful patterns, pressure shifts, and important match developments.
- Evidence Verification Agent: Checks generated interpretations against supporting match events and identifies unsupported claims.
- Narrative Agent: Converts verified insights into accessible, engaging, and personalized football stories.

Agents will share structured match context and exchange information through defined workflows. Our goal is to demonstrate meaningful collaboration rather than adding agents simply for architectural complexity.

Proposed Technology Stack

We intend to explore Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Agent Framework for model integration and agent orchestration.

Our candidate development stack includes:

- Python and FastAPI for backend services and event processing.
- TypeScript, React, or Next.js for an interactive frontend.
- Microsoft Foundry for AI model integration and evaluation.
- Microsoft Agent Framework for multi-agent workflows.
- Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions for cloud deployment.
- GitHub and GitHub Copilot for collaborative development.

The final architecture will be refined based on available resources, team expertise, and practical development constraints.

Innovation and Expected Impact

Our key differentiator is **explainable, evidence-grounded football storytelling**.

Instead of producing isolated statistics or generic AI commentary, MatchMind AI aims to connect raw events, match context, AI reasoning, and personalized presentation in a traceable workflow.

We believe this approach could benefit sports broadcasters, match analysts, digital content platforms, and fans seeking more accessible and trustworthy football insights.

Hackathon Goals

Our initial goal is to deliver a working end-to-end prototype that can:

1. Replay a realistic synthetic football event stream.
2. Calculate and update relevant match statistics.
3. Detect important match developments.
4. Generate AI-powered explanations with supporting evidence.
5. Display insights through an interactive dashboard.
6. Demonstrate personalized commentary and automated match recaps.

We will prioritize a reliable, demonstrable core experience before expanding into additional features.

All match events will be synthetic or otherwise appropriately licensed, and the project will be developed specifically for this hackathon.

title: MatchMind – AI-Powered Live Football Companion
tagline: MatchMind turns live scores into stories. It gives real-time updates, AI insights on match momentum and predictions for the final minutes, all in one clean scoreboard.
description:
The Problem

Millions of fans follow football matches on their phones while at work, travelling, or watching another game. Most of the time, all they get is a bare score line like "2–3, 85'". That number tells them nothing about the story behind it. Who is dominating possession? Is the losing team pushing for an equaliser? Was the last goal a counterattack or a penalty? How likely is a comeback in the final minutes? Today, fans have to jump between score apps, social media, and live commentary to piece this together, and many simply miss the most exciting moments of the match.

Our Solution

MatchMind is an AI-powered live match companion that turns raw scores into clear, engaging stories. Instead of just showing numbers, MatchMind explains what is happening in the match and what might happen next.

Key features:

1. Live Scoreboard: A clean, easy-to-read scoreboard showing the score, match minute, goal scorers, and key events such as cards and substitutions.

2. AI Match Insights: An AI agent built on Azure AI Foundry reads the match events and explains momentum in plain language, for example: "Riverside Athletic have had 70% of possession in the last 10 minutes and are pushing hard for an equaliser."

3. Late-Game Predictions: MatchMind estimates the chance of different outcomes in the final minutes, such as "Riverside has a 22% chance to equalise before full time," and updates these predictions as the match develops.

4. Key Moment Summaries: If a fan joins late or looks away, MatchMind gives a short catch-up summary of everything important that happened.

5. Fan Interaction: Fans can make quick predictions during the match, react to key moments, and compare their guesses with the AI and other fans.

Demo

Our demo uses sample data with fictional teams, Riverside Athletic and Northgate United, to show a dramatic late-game scenario: Northgate United leading 3–2 in the 85th minute while Riverside pushes for an equaliser. Using mock data lets us show every feature reliably during judging without depending on a live match happening at that time, and it avoids using real club names and trademarks. In production, MatchMind would connect to a live football data API to work with real matches.

How It Works

1. A match data feed sends live events (goals, shots, possession, cards, substitutions) to the MatchMind backend.
2. The backend stores the match state and passes recent events to an AI agent in Azure AI Foundry.
3. The agent analyses the events, generates plain-language insights and predictions, and returns them to the app.
4. The frontend shows the scoreboard, insights, and predictions to the fan in real time.

Tech Stack

Frontend: Web app (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
Backend: Python
AI: Azure AI Foundry agent for match commentary, insights, and predictions
Data: Mock match feed for the demo, with a live sports data API planned for production

Goals

1. Make live football matches easier and more exciting to follow on any screen.
2. Show how AI agents can add real context and storytelling to real-time sports data.
3. Help fans who join late or cannot watch catch up quickly on what matters.
4. Build a flexible base that can be extended to other sports and to esports.

Synthetic Match Data

MatchMind includes a synthetic match engine that generates realistic football matches from scratch. It creates fictional teams, players, and full event timelines (goals, shots, possession changes, cards, and substitutions) that follow real football patterns. This lets us test and demonstrate the insights engine on unlimited match scenarios, including rare situations like late comebacks, red cards, and penalty shootouts, without needing licensed real-world data. The same insights engine can later run on real Premier League data with no changes to the AI layer.

Future Plans

1. Connect to live football data from major leagues.
2. Add support for more languages so fans worldwide can use MatchMind.
3. Offer personalised insights based on a fan's favourite team.
4. Expand to other sports such as cricket, basketball, and esports tournaments.

title: MatchMind: A Live Multi-Agent AI Match Companion
tagline: Synthetic match events stream through Azure into a team of Foundry agents that spot key moments, explain why they matter, and deliver personalized live commentary and overlay cards for every kind of fan.
description:
## Overview
MatchMind is a live AI match companion. A synthetic match engine streams football events through an Azure pipeline into a team of specialized AI agents. The agents spot the moments that matter, explain *why* they matter, and turn them into personalized commentary and broadcast-ready overlay cards for each viewer.

It covers all five stages of the challenge: **ingest, interpret, explain, render and personalize**.

## How it works
**1. Synthetic match engine (data)**
A Python simulator generates a realistic 90-minute match as a stream of events: passes, shots, tackles, pressing actions and possession changes. Each event has a timestamp, x/y pitch coordinates, player, team and outcome. Players have simple traits (passing accuracy, speed, pressing tendency) so the stats look believable. The generator is published in the repo so others can reuse it. All clubs and players are fictional.

**2. Live pipeline (Azure cloud-native)**
The simulator streams events into Azure Event Hubs. Azure Functions / Container Apps compute rolling stats: possession, xG, pass difficulty, pressing intensity and momentum.

**3. Multi-agent layer (Microsoft Foundry / Agent Framework)**
Specialized agents share live match state:
- **Stats agent**: spots notable moments, such as an xG spike or a run of 10+ passes.
- **Tactics agent**: explains why a moment matters (e.g. "The high press has forced 4 turnovers in 6 minutes; control is shifting").
- **Narrator agent**: writes live commentary lines and a full-time recap.
- **Personalization agent**: rewrites output for each viewer's mode, club, favorite player and language.
- **Orchestrator**: routes work between agents and falls back gracefully if an agent fails.

**4. On-screen output (rendering)**
Agents emit timed JSON overlay cards, the format a broadcaster's graphics system could consume. A web app shows a 2D pitch view with the ball's position, pass arrows, shot and tackle markers, and AI cards appearing in sync. Playback speed controls (10x/30x) and a scrub bar let viewers jump to key moments.

**5. Personalization**
The same moment, told differently for each fan:
- *Analyst mode*: "Pass, 34m, difficulty 0.82, through 2 lines."
- *Casual fan mode, in Spanish, following a favorite player*: a short, excited line about the same pass.

## Goals
- Show how a multi-agent system can turn raw match data into explanations, not just stats.
- Deliver personalized, multilingual commentary from one shared data stream.
- Provide a reusable synthetic match data generator for the community.
- Build a resilient, cloud-native pipeline on Azure with clear documentation and an architecture diagram.

description:
## What it does
MatchMind is an AI broadcast booth for football. A team of specialised agents turns a live stream of match events into explainable match intelligence: timed overlay cards that explain **why** a moment matters, personalised for each viewer.

- **Stats agent** computes every number in code through an **MCP** server (possession, xG, pressure, momentum, control vs chaos). Numbers never come from an LLM.
- **Producer** routes each moment by importance: goals get the full team, routine moments get templates. A circuit breaker protects against outages.
- **Insight** and **Narrator** agents explain the moment and commentate; the Narrator writes the full-time recap.
- **Personalizer** rewrites every card for fans or analysts, in English, Urdu and Arabic, around your favourite club and player.
- **Verifier** (no LLM) checks every answer against the facts: wrong numbers, invented players or a wrong scoreline are sent back for a retry.
- **Ask MatchMind:** a **GitHub Copilot** agent answers viewer questions by calling the same MCP stats tools, locked to read-only access.

When models fail, the system recovers visibly: retry with feedback, then the next model, down to **Microsoft Foundry Local** on-device, then verified templates. Every handoff is logged in a debug drawer.

## Microsoft technology
- **Microsoft Agent Framework (Python):** workflow orchestration, agents with structured output, MCP client, WorkflowViz, DevUI
- **GitHub Copilot SDK** via Agent Framework's GitHubCopilotAgent
- **Microsoft Foundry Local:** on-device model in the fallback chain (Phi-3.5-mini supported)
- **Model Context Protocol**, **GitHub Codespaces**, **GitHub Actions**

## Try it (2 minutes, browser only)
1. Open https://alisaeed-1.github.io/matchmind/
2. Pick **Rivermouth Rovers v Ironmere Athletic** and press play.
3. Switch **Fan / Analyst**, change language with the tune icon, open the hub icon to see agent handoffs, and the speech-bubble icon to see Copilot answers.

Live agents: open the repo in GitHub Codespaces (one click from the README).

**Video:** https://youtu.be/4vEOSFYaHo4

# MatchPointAI — Explainable Football Match Intelligence

**MatchPointAI transforms football match events into real-time, explainable intelligence using Microsoft Azure and AI.**

## The Problem

Traditional football scoreboards and statistical dashboards tell viewers what happened, but rarely explain why it matters. Fans, broadcasters, and analysts need accessible insights into momentum shifts, attacking pressure, scoring opportunities, and decisive match events.

## Our Solution

MatchPointAI is an interactive, AI-powered football intelligence platform that combines live-style match visualization, tactical analytics, natural-language explanations, and expressive voice commentary.

The current prototype uses simulated football match data to demonstrate how AI can transform event streams into engaging, understandable match intelligence.

## Key Features

- **Live Match Visualization:** An interactive football pitch displays passes, shots, goals, and attacking movements alongside a live scoreboard and goal replay.
- **Match Pulse:** Analyzes attacking pressure, momentum, and match volatility to reveal shifts in control.
- **AI Match Commentary:** Generates context-aware commentary for important events, including scoring opportunities, sustained attacking pressure, and goals.
- **Azure AI Speech:** Converts commentary into natural-sounding audio with expressive goal announcements.
- **Explainable Key Moments:** Identifies significant events and provides evidence-backed explanations through an interactive WHY? feature.
- **Tactical Intelligence:** Analyzes attacking actions, expected goals, pressure, and momentum with supporting-event verification.
- **Ask MatchPointAI:** Allows users to explore match intelligence using natural-language questions.
- **AI Storyteller:** Produces narrative analysis of match developments.

## Microsoft Azure Architecture

MatchPointAI uses:

- **Azure App Service** to host its Python FastAPI backend.
- **Azure Static Web Apps** to host its React frontend.
- **Azure AI Speech** for natural-sounding voice commentary.
- **Azure AI Foundry** for AI-generated match storytelling and analysis.

## Innovation and Impact

MatchPointAI goes beyond conventional sports dashboards by connecting AI-generated observations to the underlying match events that support them.

Its emphasis on explainability helps make complex football analytics more accessible and trustworthy while creating opportunities for interactive broadcasts, personalized fan experiences, and AI-assisted sports analysis.

## Current Status and Future Vision

MatchPointAI is a working, cloud-hosted prototype demonstrated with simulated football events.

Future development could include live match-data integration, multilingual commentary, additional competitions, and more advanced predictive intelligence.

## Project Links

**Live Demo:** https://orange-bay-09c579b10.4.azurestaticapps.net

**Source Code:** https://github.com/kerrya0412-source/MatchPointAI

## Watch Our Demonstration

Watch the 1-minute, 58-second MatchPointAI hackathon demo:

https://youtu.be/8Bvoz8Vh9ok

title: MatchPulse: Explainable Live Football Insights
tagline: From synthetic match events to evidence-backed stories, live overlays, and fan experiences tailored to every viewer.
description:
## What we’re building

**MatchPulse** is an AI-powered match intelligence engine that transforms synthetic, football-realistic event streams into timely, explainable stories for fans, analysts, and broadcast teams.

Rather than reporting statistics in isolation, MatchPulse identifies patterns such as rising pressure, changes in territorial control, chaotic periods, and influential player performances. It explains why those developments matter and shows the match events and metrics behind each insight.

## How it works

MatchPulse connects five stages in one pipeline:

1. **Ingest:** A repeatable synthetic match simulator generates timestamped passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, pressure events, player details, and match metadata.
2. **Interpret:** Azure Databricks processes the events and calculates rolling team and player metrics, such as possession, territory, pass quality, pressure, and shot speed.
3. **Explain:** The system detects notable patterns and creates evidence-backed explanations linked to the relevant statistics, time window, and match events.
4. **Render:** Insights appear as live match updates and timed, machine-readable JSON payloads designed for broadcast-style graphical overlays.
5. **Personalize:** Viewers can choose experiences such as a quick fan view, an analyst view, a favorite-club view, or a player-focused mode. Narratives can also be adapted for different languages.

## Example insight

Instead of only showing “Team A has 62% possession,” MatchPulse could explain:

> Team A is taking control: its share of possession in the attacking third rose from 38% to 61% over the last five minutes, followed by three shots after high regains.

A fan might see the concise version, while an analyst can inspect the supporting metrics and events.

## Technology and goals

Azure Databricks is planned as the data-processing foundation for ingesting synthetic events, calculating rolling match intelligence, and storing replayable match data and insights. An AI narrative layer will turn structured findings into clear explanations, recaps, and personalized outputs.

Our goal is to make match intelligence useful in real time: engaging for fans, informative for analysts, and structured for broadcast and streaming experiences. The project will demonstrate the full journey from synthetic event to explainable insight to audience-ready presentation.

tagline: A team of AI agents that turns live football events into commentary, tactical insights and recaps in any language, where every claim links back to the events that prove it.
description:
**Challenge: The Synthetic Match Insights Engine for Premier League Studio.**

**Live demo:** https://ca-matchroom-oy5o46jqadfro.bluebush-9765fe66.eastus2.azurecontainerapps.io/
**Code:** https://github.com/saisyalla96/matchroom

## The problem
Studios and streaming platforms want instant match stories for every fan, but an AI that invents a statistic can't go on air.

## What Matchroom does
Matchroom is a live AI match studio built on synthetic, football-realistic data. A real-time engine computes the intelligence: pass difficulty, xG, shot and ball speed, pressing intensity, momentum, and control-vs-chaos phases. It turns these into timed overlay cues, each with a plain-English "why it matters" and the IDs of the events that prove it. AI agents then write the words for each viewer, and nothing reaches the screen until a Verifier has checked it.

- **Explainable:** click any line to see why it matters, with the passes and shots behind it drawn on the pitch.
- **Personalised:** one match, five experiences: casual fan, analyst, favourite club, player focus and a single-metric tracker, in any language.
- **Trustworthy:** the Verifier is code, not AI. Every number must exist in the facts with the right unit, every player named must be in the moment, and text must be in the right script. In a fault-injection test it caught 32 of 32 deliberately corrupted lines; across 168 real lines it made no false blocks.
- **Measured:** the simulator records hidden tactical ground truth, so explanations are scored. Pressing-surge explanations are right 53% of the time versus about 20% by chance, over 20 matches.

## Built with
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service (three versioned agents on gpt-5.4-mini), Azure Container Apps with a managed identity (no keys), Application Insights and OpenTelemetry tracing visible in Foundry Traces, Bicep and the Azure Developer CLI (one-command deploy), and GitHub Actions CI.

## Data
All clubs, players and matches are fictional and generated by our own simulator, which also serves as a reusable labelled dataset. No real Premier League data is used.

title: MatchShift

description:
# MatchShift

**60-second guided demo:** https://matchshift-pd.azurewebsites.net/?demo=judge  
**Live application:** https://matchshift-pd.azurewebsites.net/  
**Source code:** https://github.com/pdidow/MatchShift *(private for now; will be made public before the submission deadline)*  
*The Azure App Service uses a free tier, so the first request after inactivity may take a few seconds to wake.*

**Football intelligence you can question, verify, and replay.**

MatchShift transforms live, synthetic football events into meaningful, explainable match intelligence for fans, analysts and broadcasters.

The current hosted application combines a shared guided judge experience, six-language presentation and narration, a real Accessibility Center, synchronized timeline-aware speech, 3D Evidence Replay with a performance-aware reactive stadium crowd, and visible multi-agent verification.

Instead of simply reporting what happened, MatchShift detects meaningful changes in pressure, territory, passing patterns, attacking direction, possession quality and match control — then explains **why those changes matter**.

The core principle is simple:

> **AI does not decide what happened in the match. The match data does.**

MatchShift's deterministic analytics remain the authoritative source of football facts. They identify meaningful changes, calculate metrics, enforce thresholds and sample requirements, and retain the source events behind every insight.

Microsoft Agent Framework then orchestrates specialized AI agents that interpret those grounded facts, adapt the explanation for different audiences, create accessible narration and independently verify the result before it is presented to the viewer.

This keeps a clear distinction between what the data proves and what AI believes the data may mean.

Every important insight can be challenged.

Viewers can select:

- **WHY?** — Inspect the metrics, thresholds, sample sizes, confidence and evidence behind the insight.
- **SHOW ME** — Jump directly to the supporting source events, with contextual events clearly separated from evidence.
- **EVIDENCE REPLAY** — Reconstruct the important sequence in 3D from multiple tactical viewpoints, compare the match state before and after the detected shift, and place the evidence inside a performance-aware stadium scene with an optional reactive crowd.
- **AGENTS** — Inspect how the deterministic engine, Microsoft Agent Framework agents, grounding checks and Verification Agent produced the final result.

MatchShift explicitly separates:

- **FACT** — what the match data proves
- **INFERENCE** — what the evidence suggests
- **POSSIBLE EXPLANATION** — a plausible tactical interpretation that is not presented as fact

---

## 60-second guided judge demo

The live application includes an optional guided demo designed to expose MatchShift's strongest features without hiding the real product.

Both entry points — the direct `?demo=judge` URL and the in-product **Guided demo · 60 s** button — use the same guided sequence.

Before the flagship insight, the guide now includes a concise **Built for every viewer** step. It highlights the real language selector and the real Accessibility Center, names all six supported languages, and lets the viewer open the Accessibility Center without silently changing any settings.

Supported languages are:

- English
- French
- Spanish
- German
- Italian
- European Portuguese

The guide then takes the viewer through a real flagship insight:

**63′ — Westhaven switch their attack down the right**

The underlying deterministic evidence shows the right-sided share of the attack increasing from **31% to 90%**, with a **z-score of 3.29**, High confidence and **30 supporting events**.

The guided path is:

```text
INTRO
      ↓
BUILT FOR EVERY VIEWER
      ↓
FLAGSHIP INSIGHT
      ↓
WHY?
      ↓
SHOW ME
      ↓
EVIDENCE REPLAY
      ↓
AGENT WORKFLOW
      ↓
VERIFICATION + EVALUATION PROOF
```

The guide uses the real MatchShift application, real synthetic match state, real accessibility controls and real evidence chain. Evidence Replay also uses the real stadium scene, including the optional crowd layer. It can be exited at any time, leaving the viewer free to use MatchShift normally.

The message is deliberate: **the wording changes; the evidence does not.**

---

## Evidence means evidence

MatchShift distinguishes between events that **support** an insight and events shown only as **context**.

For the flagship attack-channel shift:

- **30 events** are authoritative supporting evidence.
- **1 additional event** is shown as grey context for comparison.
- The contextual event is **not counted as evidence**.
- WHY?, SHOW ME, Evidence Replay, broadcast overlays and exported demo data all use the same evidence/context split.

This distinction matters because MatchShift is designed to let the viewer inspect the exact evidence behind an AI interpretation rather than trusting a black box.

---

## Real Microsoft multi-agent orchestration

MatchShift uses a genuine Microsoft Agent Framework workflow backed by Microsoft Foundry and `gpt-4.1-mini`.

The workflow begins only after MatchShift's deterministic engine identifies a meaningful insight candidate. Raw match events are not sent blindly through AI.

```text
Synthetic Match Events
        ↓
Deterministic MatchShift Analytics
        ↓
Meaningful Insight Candidate
        ↓
Grounded InsightContext
        ↓
Tactical Analyst Agent
        ↓
   ┌────┴────┐
   ↓         ↓
Audience   Accessibility
Narrative  Narrator
   └────┬────┘
        ↓
Deterministic Grounding Validation
        ↓
Verification Agent
        ↓
Final Deterministic Validation
        ↓
APPROVED / APPROVED WITH CHANGES / REJECTED
```

### Tactical Analyst Agent

The Tactical Analyst interprets the deterministic evidence.

It can explain what a change may mean tactically, identify patterns and suggest possible explanations, but it cannot alter the authoritative match facts.

### Audience Narrative Agent

The Audience Narrative Agent explains the same grounded insight differently depending on who is watching.

A casual fan may want a simple story.

A learner may want football terminology explained.

An analyst may want the numbers and tactical implications.

A broadcaster may want a concise, presentation-ready narrative.

**The wording changes. The evidence does not.**

### Accessibility Narrator Agent

The Accessibility Narrator creates an accessible version of the same grounded intelligence for nonvisual and simplified experiences.

It supports spoken insights, plain-language explanations, visual descriptions and audio descriptions of Evidence Replay.

The Audience Narrative and Accessibility Narrator can run concurrently, then rejoin the workflow before verification.

### Verification Agent

The Verification Agent independently checks generated interpretation and narration against the grounded match context.

It can return:

- **APPROVED**
- **APPROVED WITH CHANGES**
- **REJECTED**

A rejected result is not silently published as verified intelligence.

---

## Deterministic validation around AI

MatchShift does not rely on one AI model to police another.

Deterministic code validates generated output before and after AI verification.

It checks things such as:

- evidence IDs
- numerical claims
- score
- match time
- players
- source events
- thresholds
- sample requirements
- future-event references
- unsupported causal claims
- evidence/context separation

If an AI-generated claim conflicts with the authoritative match state, MatchShift can reject or remove it even if the AI verifier approves it.

This produces a clear chain of trust:

```text
Deterministic Facts
        ↓
AI Interpretation
        ↓
Deterministic Grounding Check
        ↓
AI Verification
        ↓
Final Deterministic Check
        ↓
Verified Insight
```

This is not theoretical. During live hosted Foundry runs, MatchShift's deterministic validation has removed unsupported generated claims before publication while leaving the authoritative match facts unchanged.

---

## Microsoft Foundry Evaluations

MatchShift also measures the quality of its AI output with real Microsoft Foundry Evaluations.

A completed evaluation run tested **39 rows** across English, French and Spanish using `gpt-4.1-mini` as the evaluation judge.

That published Foundry evaluation snapshot predates the later German, Italian and European Portuguese expansion. The product now supports six languages; the added languages are covered by the application's deterministic grounding and regression tests, while the published Foundry evaluation numbers below remain the original English/French/Spanish run.

For the **28 published outputs**:

| Evaluation | Result |
|---|---:|
| Groundedness | **4.89 / 5 — 28/28 passing** |
| Relevance | **4.93 / 5 — 28/28 passing** |
| Coherence | **4.11 / 5 — 28/28 passing** |

The evaluation suite also contains deliberately injected defects such as incorrect scores, unsupported percentages, invented players, invented event IDs, future events, invented match times, unsupported player counts and causal overclaims.

Catch results:

| Quality layer | Injected defects caught |
|---|---:|
| Deterministic MatchShift validator | **11 / 11** |
| Verification Agent | **11 / 11** |
| Foundry groundedness evaluator | **5 / 11** |

This result reinforces the architecture rather than replacing it: generic AI evaluation is useful for measuring quality, but exact football facts remain protected by deterministic validation.

The evaluation suite also covers audience consistency, accessibility output and multilingual fact preservation.

---

## Different viewers. Same evidence.

The same match can become different experiences without changing the underlying truth.

A casual fan might see:

> **"Westhaven are beginning to take control down the right."**

A learner can ask why and receive a plain-language explanation.

An analyst can inspect the underlying changes in progression, territory and pressure.

A broadcaster can receive a concise narrative suitable for an on-screen graphic.

A visually impaired viewer can hear an accessible description of both the insight and Evidence Replay.

All of them receive different presentations of the **same grounded match state**.

The same grounded intelligence can also be presented in **English, French, Spanish, German, Italian or European Portuguese** without changing the underlying evidence.

---

## Evidence, not just answers

MatchShift is designed so viewers do not have to trust a black box.

An insight is only the beginning.

The viewer can move through the complete evidence chain:

```text
INSIGHT
   ↓
WHY?
   ↓
SHOW ME
   ↓
EVIDENCE REPLAY
```

**WHY?** explains the metrics, thresholds, confidence and reasoning.

**SHOW ME** identifies the supporting source events and clearly separates contextual events that are shown only for comparison.

**EVIDENCE REPLAY** reconstructs the sequence so the viewer can inspect what happened for themselves.

### Reactive stadium atmosphere

Evidence Replay also includes an optional, performance-aware stadium crowd layer designed to make the reconstruction feel like a football match without turning presentation into evidence.

The crowd is deliberately lightweight:

- spectators are rendered with instanced low-poly geometry rather than individual animated characters;
- crowd density scales between **Off**, **Low** and **Normal** modes according to device capability and user choice;
- on capable hardware, **Normal** mode can use short deterministic group reactions to important replay events such as goals, shots, interceptions, recoveries and turnovers;
- routine events do not trigger unnecessary crowd movement;
- **Low** mode remains intentionally static to protect performance;
- Reduced Motion disables crowd reactions;
- a runtime performance guard can disable automatically selected crowd rendering if replay performance degrades;
- the crowd never contributes to evidence counts, supporting-event IDs, context-event IDs, narration claims or agent reasoning.

This separation is intentional: **the crowd adds atmosphere; the match events remain the evidence.** Evidence markers, replay cameras, source events and accessibility information always take priority over stadium decoration.

The goal is not simply to generate football commentary.

The goal is to make AI football intelligence **explainable, challengeable and verifiable**.

---

## Built on Microsoft technology

MatchShift currently uses:

- Microsoft Agent Framework
- Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows
- Microsoft Foundry
- Microsoft Foundry Evaluations
- `gpt-4.1-mini`
- Azure App Service
- Azure Managed Identity
- ASP.NET Core
- React
- TypeScript
- deterministic C# match analytics

The live application is hosted on Azure App Service.

The hosted MatchShift backend authenticates to Microsoft Foundry using a system-assigned managed identity rather than API keys or user credentials.

The live execution path is:

```text
Browser
   ↓
Azure App Service
   ↓
MatchShift ASP.NET Backend
   ↓
Microsoft Agent Framework
   ↓
System-Assigned Managed Identity
   ↓
Microsoft Foundry
   ↓
gpt-4.1-mini
```

MatchShift exposes safe workflow traces showing which stages ran, which agents participated, the model used, handoffs, concurrency, timings, grounding checks and the final verification decision.

This makes the multi-agent architecture visible rather than asking judges to take it on faith.

---

## Proven hosted execution

MatchShift's Microsoft stack has been tested end to end through the public Azure-hosted application.

Hosted workflows have successfully executed:

1. Tactical Analyst Agent
2. Audience Narrative Agent
3. Accessibility Narrator Agent
4. Verification Agent

The Audience Narrative and Accessibility branches execute concurrently, then rejoin before deterministic grounding and verification.

A live workflow exposes truthful runtime status including:

- `LIVE_FOUNDRY`
- Microsoft Agent Framework
- Microsoft Foundry
- `gpt-4.1-mini`
- system-assigned managed identity
- verification result
- no API keys
- no stored client secrets
- no dependency on a developer's local Azure login

The final result is published as verified intelligence only after the deterministic and AI verification layers complete successfully.

---

## Execution modes

MatchShift clearly distinguishes between three execution modes.

### LIVE_FOUNDRY

A real Microsoft Agent Framework workflow runs against Microsoft Foundry.

### OFFLINE_TEMPLATE

A deterministic fallback is used when live AI is unavailable.

Offline output is never presented as live Foundry output or verified live AI.

### RECORDED_DEMO

Previously captured live workflow results can be replayed for static demonstration.

Recorded demonstrations are clearly labelled and are not presented as live execution.

---

## Accessibility is part of the architecture

Accessibility is not an afterthought or a separate simplified version of MatchShift.

The same grounded match intelligence can be transformed for different accessibility needs while preserving the underlying evidence and meaning.

Narration automatically follows the viewer's selected language and uses a matching browser/device voice when available, with graceful same-language fallback when an exact regional voice is unavailable. Spoken insights, accessibility narration and Evidence Replay descriptions therefore stay aligned with the language selected in MatchShift rather than defaulting back to English.

Current accessibility capabilities include:

- spoken insights
- audio match mode
- six-language interface and narration: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian and European Portuguese
- visual descriptions
- plain-language explanations
- Evidence Replay audio description
- captions and transcript support
- high contrast
- colour-vision support
- reduced motion and reduced flashing
- enlarged text
- keyboard navigation
- simplified insight presentation

### Speech follows the timeline

MatchShift does not try to make speech run at the same speed as accelerated match playback.

Instead, narration remains human-intelligible and follows the authoritative match clock:

- at **1×**, MatchShift can provide fuller useful narration;
- at the default **2×**, it uses concise, current narration and drops stale cues instead of building a backlog;
- at **5×**, narration becomes more selective;
- at **10×**, only critical events and structural match moments are prioritized.

Goals, half-time and full-time are protected from being silently lost. The narration queue remains bounded, stale commentary is discarded rather than spoken late, and playback speed never blindly multiplies the user's speech rate.

### Evidence Replay owns the audio

When Evidence Replay opens, MatchShift pauses the underlying match, cancels normal match narration and gives the replay exclusive MatchShift audio focus.

Replay descriptions follow the replay timeline rather than a separate wall-clock queue. Pausing, seeking or restarting the replay clears narration that is no longer relevant. When Evidence Replay closes, the previous match play/pause state and playback speed are restored, but interrupted old commentary is **not** resumed.

Crowd reactions remain visual only and do not compete with Evidence Replay narration. Reduced Motion keeps the crowd static, and the crowd layer never changes the evidence or the spoken interpretation of that evidence.

This keeps the spoken description aligned with what the viewer is actually seeing.

The Accessibility Narrator is a real participant in the multi-agent workflow rather than a post-processing label attached to the UI. It receives the same grounded match context as the other agents and produces an accessible version of the same verified intelligence without changing the underlying facts.

---

## Current regression proof

The current guided-demo build is covered by a broad local regression suite:

- **437 .NET tests passing**
- **164 web tests passing**
- clean TypeScript type-check
- successful production web build

The hosted Azure deployment has also been smoke-tested for health, managed-identity Foundry status, both guided-demo entry points, all six language options, the real Accessibility Center, the flagship WHY?/SHOW ME/Evidence Replay flow, the optional stadium crowd layer, and synchronized narration behavior.

---

## Why MatchShift

Most football applications tell the viewer what happened.

MatchShift goes further.

It detects change.

It explains the significance.

It adapts that explanation to the viewer.

It verifies the AI.

It measures the quality of that AI with Microsoft Foundry Evaluations.

And then it exposes the evidence.

MatchShift does not ask:

> **"Do you trust the AI?"**

It asks:

> **"Do you want to see why?"**

title: MatchSight AI: Hidden Match Reconstruction & Tactical Intelligence
tagline: See beyond the camera. Reconstruct hidden players, uncover tactical shifts, and explain why every key moment matters.
description:
MatchSight AI is an AI-powered football intelligence engine that reconstructs the match beyond what the broadcast camera shows. It combines player tracking, computer vision, spatial reconstruction, and tactical analysis to turn raw match footage and tracking data into an explainable account of how a game unfolds.

Traditional football analytics can tell us what happened. MatchSight AI aims to explain how player positioning and tactical changes shaped what happened next.

Key Capabilities:

1. Hidden Player Reconstruction
The system estimates the pitch positions of players who disappear from the broadcast camera, using available observations, temporal movement patterns, and team-shape information. Predictions include confidence and uncertainty, allowing viewers to distinguish observed positions from inferred ones.

2. Tactical Intelligence
The engine analyzes spatial and temporal patterns, including possession, territorial control, team width and compactness, pressing intensity, defensive structure, transitions, and potential tactical shifts.

3. Evidence-Based Match Stories
Instead of presenting isolated statistics, MatchSight AI connects important events with changes in player positioning, tactical state, and subsequent outcomes. Its Match Story concept organizes these relationships into an interpretable timeline of the match.

4. Interactive Match Exploration
The application combines pitch visualizations, reconstructed player positions, match timelines, key moments, and tactical explanations in a unified studio interface.

Technical Approach:

The project combines a Python and FastAPI backend with a Next.js and React frontend. Its computer vision pipeline uses player detection and multi-object tracking, while its reconstruction system combines spatial and temporal modelling with team-shape priors and uncertainty estimation. Ground-truth tracking data and synthetic benchmarks support controlled evaluation.

The architecture separates observed data, model-inferred positions, and reference ground truth so that reconstruction quality can be evaluated rather than assumed.

Goal and Impact:

Our goal is to help analysts, broadcasters, coaches, and football fans understand the hidden spatial context behind important match moments. By connecting player movement to tactical interpretation, MatchSight AI aims to make football analysis more visual, explainable, and accessible.

The project is being developed as a prototype, with ongoing work focused on improving reconstruction accuracy, validating tactical insights on real matches, and making the analysis more reliable and useful.

description:
# MatchMind AI - Real-Time Football Intelligence

**Every Match. Every Moment. Your Story.**

## Overview

MatchMind AI is an AI-powered, real-time football intelligence platform that transforms synthetic match events into explainable insights, personalized narratives, and broadcast-ready visual experiences.

Football is more than goals and statistics. Every pass, tackle, possession change, and tactical adjustment tells a story. MatchMind AI makes those stories accessible to fans, analysts, and broadcasters through intelligent event processing and coordinated AI agents.

## How It Works

MatchMind AI follows a five-stage intelligence pipeline:

**1. Ingest:** Process synthetic, football-realistic match events, including passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, player movements, and pressure events.

**2. Interpret:** Calculate match statistics, identify tactical patterns, detect momentum shifts, and evaluate player performance using structured event data.

**3. Explain:** Use specialized AI agents to explain why key moments matter, connecting insights to supporting match events and measurable statistics.

**4. Render:** Generate real-time visual insights, synchronized match timelines, and structured, machine-readable overlays suitable for broadcast and streaming experiences.

**5. Personalize:** Adapt match intelligence to individual audiences based on language preferences, favorite teams, selected players, and viewing modes.

## Core Features

### Live Match Intelligence
Real-time match event processing, tactical momentum tracking, player statistics, pressure analysis, and automated detection of significant moments.

### Multi-Agent Intelligence
Specialized Tactical, Narrative, and Audience agents collaborate to produce contextual football insights, natural-language commentary, and personalized explanations.

### Personalized Viewing Modes
- **Fan Mode:** Accessible match stories and team-focused highlights.
- **Analyst Mode:** Detailed performance metrics, tactical insights, and evidence-based explanations.
- **Broadcast Mode:** Timed, machine-readable graphics and narratives designed for live production workflows.
- **Player Focus:** Personalized tracking and storytelling around a selected player's performance.

### AI-Powered Match Recaps
Automatically generate contextual match summaries, tactical explanations, player highlights, and key-event narratives.

### Multilingual Storytelling
Deliver personalized football narratives in multiple languages, beginning with English and Turkish.

## Technology

MatchMind AI goes beyond displaying football statistics. It connects measurable events to explainable insights and transforms the same underlying match intelligence into different experiences for different audiences.

The platform is designed around synthetic football data, real-time responsiveness, transparent explanations, and extensible broadcast integrations.

**Our Vision:** Make every football match more understandable, engaging, and personal through explainable AI.

description:
MatchTurning AI

Football tells a story beyond the final score. MatchMind AI is a match intelligence studio designed to help fans, analysts and broadcasters understand what changed during a match and inspect the evidence behind each insight.

What it does

MatchMind transforms original, synthetic football events into an interactive match experience featuring:

- Connected passing sequences, possession changes, tackles and shots.
- A pitch visualization with playback controls and timeline navigation.
- Transparent team statistics and player performance summaries.
- Detection of changes in pressure activity and chance creation.
- Before-and-after comparisons with supporting event IDs and replayable evidence.
- Fan and analyst explanations, team preferences, key moments and match recaps.

Its central feature asks: “Why did the match change?” Viewers can inspect a detected shift, compare the underlying statistics and replay the relevant passage. Explanations distinguish measured changes from possible interpretations rather than presenting correlation as a proven tactical cause.

AI approach

We are adding a local language model that selects and organizes verified match facts into audience-specific commentary. The backend validates its selections and renders approved statements, with a clearly labeled fallback when inference is unavailable or fails validation.

This constrained approach prioritizes factual reliability and traceability. Local model setup and live inference evaluation are currently in progress. Microsoft Foundry integration is planned and has not yet been deployed.

Technology

The working application uses Python, Fast API, Web Sockets and a React/Vite frontend. Reproducible match seeds and automated tests support validation of simulation behavior, statistics, evidence and replay functionality.

Goals

Our goal is an accessible, reliable football storytelling tool for fans and broadcast teams: one match, different viewing experiences, and explanations that can be checked.

The project uses fictional teams and original synthetic data. It does not use real match footage or claim that its illustrative shot-quality heuristic is calibrated expected goals.

title: Matchweave AI
tagline: Evidence you can see. Stories made for you.
description:
Football fans see the score, but understanding why a match is changing requires context. Analysts need supporting evidence, while broadcast producers need concise graphics they can time and reuse. MatchWeave AI connects these needs through one workflow: ingest, interpret, explain, render and personalize.
The application processes 9,887 reproducible synthetic events across five fictional matches. Seven views support match replay, tactical exploration, player focus, automated recaps, agent inspection, broadcast graphics and historical analysis. Fans, analysts and producers receive different presentations of the same verified facts, with English, Hindi and Spanish templates and club/player preferences.
Microsoft Agent Framework coordinates specialist agents through parallel analysis, shared results, numerical verification and conditional repair. Microsoft Foundry Local runs the pretrained Qwen2.5 1.5B language model on the computer, without a paid cloud-model API. The agents select constrained claims and layouts; canonical event calculations check numerical claims before publication. Viewers can inspect the supporting event IDs and see an intentionally incorrect claim rejected, repaired and checked again. The studio exports timed JSON containing the approved facts and evidence for graphics workflows.
A separate Real match lab includes 12,372 completed results, plus two cancelled fixtures, from January 2021 through 2025–26 across the European big five leagues and Champions League, Europa League and Conference League. Qualifying rounds and 2026–27 are excluded. A locally trained logistic-regression model estimates home-win, draw and away-win probabilities from pre-match features. Its frozen evaluation model achieved 52.17% accuracy on 2,283 held-out 2025–26 matches, compared with a 45.38% frequency baseline. Historical results remain separate from synthetic tactical events.
The React/TypeScript frontend connects to a FastAPI/Python backend. Fresh local language-model inference, recorded AI runs and deterministic verification are explicitly labeled. The default demo includes recorded local-model traces and fresh historical-model inference; optional Foundry setup enables new language-model calls. Executed checks include 45 backend tests, 12 browser journeys and five health-ping checks. Source, datasets, model weights, setup instructions, reports and the 105-second demonstration are included in the public repository.

title: Momentum Ledger
tagline: An AI engine on Azure that measures how much every moment changes a match, explains why it matters, verifies every claim before it goes on screen, and tells the story differently for every fan, in any language.
description:
## The Problem
Live AI commentary is powerful, but broadcasters can't risk it on air. One invented stat on a live broadcast damages trust. Most match data tools also report *what* happened, not *why it mattered*, and they give every viewer the same experience.

## Solution
**Momentum Ledger** turns synthetic football events into explainable, verified, personalized match intelligence for studio, broadcast, and streaming.

### 1. Ingest
A synthetic match simulator streams football-realistic events (passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, pressure events, match metadata) in real time. Team styles such as high press or low block shape the event patterns, so tactical shifts emerge naturally.

### 2. Interpret
A live game-state engine computes threat by pitch zone, pressure intensity, passing tempo, pass difficulty, and control vs. chaos, so every event gets a measurable impact on the match.

### 3. Explain
Instead of narrating every event, Momentum Ledger highlights the moments that changed the game, and the points where the game itself changed character, with the reasoning behind them.

### 4. Verify and Render
Every generated insight is grounded in the underlying match data and checked before it is shown. Outputs are timecoded, machine-readable overlay data ready to sit alongside a live match feed.

### 5. Personalize
The same verified intelligence becomes different experiences:
- **Analyst mode:** deeper stats and tactical context
- **Casual mode:** the story in plain language
- **Club mode:** framed around your team
- **Player Lens:** follow one player all match
- **Catch Me Up:** joined late? Get a short recap of what mattered, from your perspective
- **Any language:** global storytelling, including underserved markets

## Goals
- Make AI match insights trustworthy enough for live production
- Explain the game beyond the scoreline
- Make every match feel made for every fan

## With
Azure OpenAI, Azure Event Hubs, Azure Functions, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure AI Translator, Python, and a web-based overlay renderer.

description:
Football stories do not end with the scoreline, and many fans in East Africa follow the game through Swahili radio commentary that digital products rarely match. Msimulizi ("the narrator") is an AI-powered match intelligence system that turns a stream of synthetic football events into live, explainable commentary, timed overlay cards and an automated full-time recap, written natively in Swahili, English and French.

The Verifier agent checks each claim against the event record and blocks anything ungrounded, with a deterministic fallback so the feed never stalls.

Every viewer gets a different experience from the same intelligence: analyst or casual fan mode, a favourite club that shifts the framing, a favourite player followed through the match, a single metric to focus on, and an audio-only radio mode for low bandwidth. Output is machine-readable JSON timed to the match clock, so it can drive broadcast overlays as well as our web viewer, and every Swahili line comes with an English gloss.

All data is synthetic. A seeded match generator with scripted storylines (a comeback, a red card, a late equaliser) produces football-realistic events with fictional clubs and players, so every demo is reproducible.

It is built on Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure AI Speech, Azure AI Content Safety, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Container Apps, Azure Blob Storage and Application Insights, with a Model Context Protocol server that exposes live match state to other agents.

title: My project idea: MatchMind AI — The AI Football Analyst
tagline: Don't just see the score. Understand the story behind the game.
description:
MatchMind AI is a multi-agent football intelligence platform that turns live (synthetic) match events into real-time, explainable “what’s happening and why” insights—then rewrites the same verified facts into audience-specific narratives for **fans**, **analysts**, and **broadcasters**.

### Problem
Most football dashboards are rich in numbers (possession, shots, passes) but poor at answering the questions people actually have during a match:
- **Why did momentum change?**
- **What is actually happening right now?**
- **What evidence supports that interpretation?**

This gap is growing as event-streaming sports data becomes commoditized; the differentiator is no longer access to stats, but **interpretation and trust**—especially in second-screen experiences and live media.

### Target users
- **Fans (primary anchor):** want instant, easy-to-understand explanations without having to interpret dashboards.
- **Broadcast/production teams:** need fast, “ready-to-say” commentary lines grounded in evidence.
- **Analysts/coaches:** want explainable tactical patterns with supporting metrics for halftime or post-match review.

### Solution (what MatchMind does)
MatchMind converts raw event streams into a transparent chain of reasoning:

**Football event stream → pattern detection → tactical interpretation → evidence → grounded explanation → personalized narrative**

Core live experience includes:
- Live score + clock + momentum visualization
- **AI Momentum Alerts** when a meaningful shift is detected (with confidence)
- A **“Why did this happen?”** drill-down screen showing the evidence window (e.g., possession change, attacks, shots, zone concentration)
- Audience mode switch: **FAN / ANALYST / BROADCASTER** narratives generated from the *same verified insight*

### Why multi-agent orchestration matters (hackathon fit)
MatchMind’s key differentiator is a **specialized, coordinated multi-agent system** that produces a better result than a single agent:

1) **Match Observer Agent**  
Ingests incoming events, flags significance, and proposes early pattern candidates.

2) **Tactical Analyst Agent**  
Compares rolling match windows (e.g., last 10 minutes vs previous 10) to detect patterns like momentum shifts and produces structured evidence + confidence.

3) **Explanation (Explainability) Agent**  
Generates a natural-language “why” explanation that is **strictly evidence-grounded**. If evidence is insufficient, it says so.

4) **Storyteller Agent**  
Rewrites the verified insight into audience-specific outputs:
- FAN: energetic and simple  
- ANALYST: metric-driven and concise  
- BROADCASTER: speakable 15–20 second commentary

The agents coordinate via a **shared match state** and visible handoffs, and the demo includes a **simulated failure + recovery** (e.g., Tactical Agent timeout → retry → recovered → insight produced) to demonstrate resilience.

### Data approach (synthetic + football-realistic)
To comply with hackathon requirements, MatchMind uses **synthetic but realistic** football events and scripted match phases to reliably produce a detectable “momentum shift” (e.g., dominance changes across minutes 60–75). This ensures the AI has a clear story to discover and explain, without relying on real redistributed match data.

### Technical approach (high-level)
- Event streaming: synthetic events ingested via an event stream, processed serverlessly, and stored for replay/recap.
- Agents: built and orchestrated with Microsoft’s agent tooling and deployed in a managed environment with observability.
- App: API + database for match state/insights + a lightweight UI focused on 5 high-quality screens (Live Match, Explainability, Agent Activity, Audience Mode, Match Recap).

### Success metrics (what judges will see)
- **Speed + clarity:** an insight appears within a target latency after an event spike, with a clear evidence timeline.
- **Trustworthiness:** “0 hallucinated stats” demonstrated via an evidence panel that only cites supplied windows/metrics, plus automated checks.
- **Multi-agent value:** a visible agent activity screen showing distinct roles, shared state, handoffs, and failure recovery.

### Expected impact
MatchMind helps fans understand the story behind the game in real time, helps broadcasters speak with confidence and accuracy under time pressure, and helps analysts quickly validate tactical shifts with transparent evidence—turning commoditized event streams into trusted, explainable match intelligence.
