title: Roar — From Fan Phones to Live Match Moments, Powered by Microsoft Foundry
tagline: Fans film the match; AI finds the moments. Roar turns every camera, big or ti into a stadium camera: Microsoft Foundry agents classify each upload, cluster clips into live Moments for broadcast and second-screen feeds, and route safety reports to the right people. Moderated, on Azure.
description:
**Fans capture the most dramatic seconds of a football match, but that footage dies on their phones. Roar turns every fan's phone into a stadium camera: uploads are understood by AI agents, grouped into shareable Moments, and pushed to a live, moderated feed for broadcast and second-screen experiences.**

## The problem
Clubs, broadcasters and streaming platforms sit on thousands of fan clips per match but can't use them at scale: content has to be classified, deduplicated, grouped by event, checked for safety, and bounded by privacy. Existing tools can store media — they can't understand it or route it safely.

## How it works
- A fan captures a photo or video while a synthetic Premier League-style match replays live through the API.
- **Moment Analyst** (Microsoft Foundry, structured outputs) classifies each clip: what happened, which match minute, confidence and reasoning — goals, saves, celebrations, fouls, incidents.
- **Storyteller** drafts the fan-facing title and description.
- A clustering engine merges same-event clips from different fans into one ranked **Moment** and promotes it to the live feed.
- **Safety Analyst** triages SOS reports and flagged media into incidents with severity, routed to the security console (state machine: reported → acknowledged → resolved; opt-in only).
- An admin and security console handles media approval, incident response and replay control.

## Explainable and safe by design
- Every AI decision persists its confidence, reasoning and lifecycle status (queued/running/done/failed/skipped), so a human can retry or override it.
- Audience ACLs: community clips go public only after moderator approval; owner-only and staff-only media are never sent to AI and never served publicly.
- No training on user media; SOS is receipt-only — a reference and an emergency number, never false promises.

## Built on Microsoft Azure
- **Microsoft Foundry** (`gpt-5-mini`) for multimodal moment analysis and safety triage over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- **Azure Container Apps** for the API, fan web app and admin console — HTTPS, scale-to-zero
- **Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server** for media, Moments and incident state
- **Azure Blob Storage** for private media, streamed through the API's ACL layer; the API authenticates with a managed identity (no keys)
- **Azure Container Registry** for images, **Log Analytics** for logs
- A custom synthetic match engine generates realism-checked football events (passes, xG shots, pressing), so the product runs with zero licensed data

## Status
Runs end-to-end: upload → AI analysis → Moment draft → moderator approval → public feed; SOS → severity-routed incident in the security console. Tests and CI are green across the monorepo and the stack is deployed on Azure Container Apps.

title: Sauti: One Match, Every Fan's Commentary
tagline: Sauti turns synthetic football events into verified, explainable match intelligence, then delivers it as live overlays, narratives and audio commentary personalized for analysts, casual fans, blind and partially sighted fans, and fans in any language, including Kiswahili.
description:
## The problem

Football fans already reach for a second screen during matches to look up stats, but the experience on the main screen is the same for everyone. A data-hungry analyst and a first-time fan see identical graphics. Fans who don't speak the broadcast language get commentary only on select fixtures. Blind and partially sighted fans have audio-described commentary mainly through stadium headsets, and at home they get commentary that comments on the action without describing it. Fans with expensive mobile data often follow matches through text alerts and radio instead of video.

Generic AI commentary doesn't fix this, because a single wrong goalscorer on air destroys trust.

## What Sauti does

Sauti ("voice" in Kiswahili) takes one stream of match events and produces many verified, personalized experiences from it, live:

- **Analyst mode:** pass difficulty, shot and sprint speeds, pressure shifts, control-vs-chaos index, with a "why are we saying this" trail behind every graphic
- **Casual mode:** plain-language storytelling that explains why a moment matters
- **Described mode:** audio commentary for blind and partially sighted fans that paints positions and movement, delivered in sync with the action
- **Player-focused mode:** the whole match told through one player you choose
- **Single-metric mode:** everything filtered through the one thing you care about, such as pressing or passing
- **Any language:** natural-language narratives and synthesized audio, starting with English and Kiswahili
- **Low-bandwidth audio mode:** the full experience without video, for fans on limited data
- **Catch-up:** a 30-second spoiler-safe briefing for fans who join mid-match
- **Automated recaps:** personalized post-match summaries in text and audio
- **Broadcast output:** timed, machine-readable overlay instructions a production team can approve and render on a live feed

## How it works: one pipeline, five stages

1. **Ingest:** a synthetic match simulator streams player and ball tracking data (10 frames per second) and derived events through Azure Event Hubs
2. **Interpret:** a deterministic stats engine computes speeds, distances, pass quality, possession, pressing intensity and match rhythm. The AI never calculates a number
3. **Explain:** a team of agents detects significant moments and explains why they matter. A verifier agent checks every claim against match state before it can air
4. **Render:** a director agent decides what goes on screen and when, emitting a timed overlay spec plus synthesized audio
5. **Personalize:** persona agents adapt the same verified intelligence to each fan's mode, club, player and language

## Built with Microsoft

- Microsoft Agent Framework workflows for multi-agent orchestration (moment detection, explanation, verification, personas, direction)
- Microsoft Foundry for model hosting, evaluation and tracing
- Azure Speech for multilingual and described audio, including Kenyan Kiswahili neural voices
- Azure Event Hubs, Container Apps, Web PubSub, Database for PostgreSQL (pgvector), Static Web Apps, Key Vault and Application Insights
- Infrastructure as code with Bicep and the Azure Developer CLI
- GitHub Copilot agent mode throughout development

## Data innovation

Sauti's simulator generates football-realistic tracking and event data from scripted storylines (comebacks, red cards, late winners), with a fictional squad and league so no real match data or club branding is used. As a stretch goal, we render the simulation as synthetic match video and run a detection model over it to auto-generate events, then measure that model's accuracy against perfect ground truth.

## Goals

- Every fan experiences the same match as one made for them
- Every on-screen or spoken claim is traceable to verified match data
- Accessibility and language are first-class modes, built in from the start

title: Scouter
tagline: Scout: Evidence-Backed Football Intelligence
description:
Scouter helps club analysts and scouts create **evidence-backed player evaluations** that coaches can trust and act on—especially for “hidden work” contributions that don’t show up in goals/assists.

Today, analysts can often find the right moments, but the story doesn’t connect cleanly to the underlying events/metrics, so recommendations don’t land. Scouter addresses this by making analysis **inspectable**: every insight is explicitly linked to the match evidence that supports it.

Scouter provides a dashboard that replays a match timeline and generates player contribution cards (e.g., pressing impact, ball progression, defensive actions). Each finding is clickable and traceable back to the specific supporting events in the timeline, enabling fast “show me why” validation during coach conversations.

The prototype also includes an experimental computer-vision lab where users can upload a match clip or share a browser tab/window to detect people and the ball, follow temporary visual tracks, and collect observations during a session. Historical context is powered by StatsBomb Open Data (available Premier League seasons). While live tracks are not yet linked to named players and session observations don’t train the model, the lab demonstrates a path toward combining event-based evidence with lightweight visual review.

Expected impact: faster, more credible player evaluation workflows; clearer communication from analysts to coaches; and better decisions informed by transparent, evidence-linked insights rather than opaque metrics.

title: Second Guess: The Football What-If Engine
tagline: Every match is full of moments that could have gone differently. Second Guess lets fans and experts rewind any key moment, try a different decision and see what might have happened, with the expected-goals change explained in plain language and every simulation grounded
description:
## 🔄 Second Guess — The Football What-If Engine

**What if he'd passed instead of shot?**

Every fan asks it. Every pundit argues about it. Second Guess answers it.

Second Guess is an AI agent that lets fans, pundits and studio teams rewind any key moment in a match, change the decision, and see a data-driven simulation of what might have happened next, with the difference explained in plain language.

---

### 🧩 The Problem

Expected goals (xG) tells us how good a chance *was*. It can't tell us whether a *different decision* would have been better. Today, "what if" debates in studios and fan chats rely on gut feeling and replays, not evidence.

---

### 💡 Our Solution

1. **Ask in natural language:** *"What if Ish had squared it instead of shooting?"* *"What if they'd pressed higher after 60 minutes?"*
2. **Simulate the alternative:** The agent identifies the moment, finds the realistic alternative options (passes, carries, shots) and runs many simulations of how the play could unfold from player positions in the synthetic data.
3. **Explain the difference:** It compares outcomes (*"The square pass raised the chance of scoring from 8% to 31%, because the teammate was unmarked with an open goal angle"*) and shows the alternative on an animated pitch.
4. **Personalise the view:** A *Fan mode* gives short, punchy verdicts. A *Pundit mode* gives a tactical breakdown for studio segments. Both are available in the viewer's language.

---

### ⚙️ How It Works

| Layer | What it does | Technology |
|---|---|---|
| **Event data** | Streams and stores synthetic, football-realistic events and positions | Microsoft Fabric (Eventstream, Eventhouse, Lakehouse) |
| **xG and decision models** | Scores the value of shots, passes and carries from any game state | Fabric Data Science notebooks, Azure Machine Learning |
| **Simulation engine** | Generates plausible alternative sequences and outcomes (Monte Carlo) | .NET service on Azure Container Apps |
| **What-If agent** | Parses questions, picks the moment, calls simulation tools, explains results | .NET with Microsoft.Extensions.AI + Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure OpenAI via Microsoft Foundry |
| **Fact-check layer** | Ensures every explanation matches the simulation output and source events | Foundry evaluations + grounding checks |
| **Multilingual output** | Translates and voices explanations | Azure AI Translator, Azure AI Speech |
| **Development** | Built and iterated with AI pair programming | GitHub, GitHub Copilot, GitHub Actions |

---

### 🔍 Explainable by Design

Every answer shows its working: the original decision, the alternatives considered, the simulated probabilities, and the source event IDs. Simulations are framed as estimates, not facts, so fans get evidence without false certainty.

---

### 📈 Expanding the Dataset

Every "what if" creates a new, labelled counterfactual scenario: the original game state, the alternative decision, and its simulated outcomes. Over time, Second Guess builds a growing synthetic dataset of decision outcomes. Analysts can use it to train better decision models, study tactical choices, and stress-test AI systems.

---

### ✅ How Second Guess Meets the Challenge Criteria

- **Analyze match events in real time:** Key moments are detected live and are ready for "what if" questions within seconds.
- **Generate stories and highlights:** "Alternative history" segments and recaps (*"The three decisions that cost them the match"*).
- **Explain key moments and tactical patterns:** Plain-language comparisons of decisions, positioning and options.
- **Expand datasets for AI and analytics:** Every simulation adds labelled counterfactual data.
- **Multilingual insights:** Explanations are translated and voiced for fans worldwide.
- **Personalized experiences:** Fan mode vs Pundit mode, team perspective, and detail level.

---

### 🎯 Goals

- Turn endless "what if" debates into **evidence-based conversations**.
- Give **studios and broadcasters** a ready-made segment generator for analysis shows.
- Help fans **understand decision-making**, not just outcomes.
- Build a **reusable counterfactual dataset** for football AI research.

---

### 🚀 What's Next

- **Live second-screen mode:** Fans vote on "what should he have done?" before the answer is revealed.
- **Manager decisions:** Simulate substitutions and formation changes, not just single plays.
- **Integration with Audio Eyes:** Spoken "what if" answers for visually impaired fans.

title: Second Screen: Explainable Live Match Intelligence
tagline: A multi-agent system that turns a live synthetic football match into fact-checked moments, broadcast-ready overlays, and personalized experiences, so the same match feels made for the analyst and the casual fan alike.
description:
## The problem
A scoreline tells you *what* happened. Fans, analysts, and broadcasters want to know *why it mattered*, and they each want it differently. A data-hungry analyst and a casual fan watching the same match need two genuinely different experiences, delivered live and in their own language.

## What Second Screen does
Second Screen ingests a live stream of synthetic, football-realistic match events and runs them through a five-stage pipeline:

1. **Ingest:** A custom match simulator streams passes, shots, tackles, pressure events, and possession changes into Azure Event Hubs. The simulator models tactical states, fatigue, and narrative arcs (pressing spells, momentum swings, comebacks), so the data carries real stories.
2. **Interpret:** A deterministic stats engine computes rolling possession, a pressure index, pass difficulty, xG, and momentum. The numbers come from code, not from an LLM.
3. **Explain:** Specialized agents built on Microsoft Agent Framework and Microsoft Foundry work together:
   - **Moment Detector:** flags key moments from statistical thresholds
   - **Tactical Explainer:** explains why a moment matters (control vs. chaos, pressure shifts, game rhythm)
   - **Fact-Checker:** rejects any claim that isn't grounded in specific events or stats, and sends it back for revision
   - **Recap Agent:** writes the full-time match story
4. **Render:** An Overlay Agent emits timed, machine-readable JSON cues synced to the match clock, ready to drive graphics on a live feed.
5. **Personalize:** A Persona Agent reshapes the same intelligence by viewer profile: analyst or casual mode, favorite club, player-focus mode, and preferred language.

## What makes it different
**Every sentence is traceable.** Each narrative claim links back to the event IDs and stats behind it, and the Fact-Checker enforces this before anything reaches the screen. That makes the output trustworthy enough for broadcast and studio use.

## Tech stack
- **Microsoft Foundry:** model hosting, agent tracing, and evaluation
- **Microsoft Agent Framework:** multi-agent orchestration and handoffs
- **Azure Event Hubs:** real-time event ingestion
- **Azure Cosmos DB:** shared agent state and the match timeline
- **Azure Container Apps:** scalable deployment of the simulator, stats engine, and agents
- **React:** live dashboard with a pitch view, an overlay preview, and side-by-side analyst and fan modes
- **GitHub Copilot:** used throughout development

All clubs, players, and match data are fictional and synthetically generated.

title: ShapeShift: Explainable Tactical Shape Intelligence and Live Match Predictions
tagline: An AI engine that reads how teams shape up in and out of possession, links overloads to xG across a season, and turns it into live, explained predictions and narratives for studio and streaming.
description:
## The problem
Football stories do not end at the scoreline. Broadcasters can show what happened, but explaining why a team is winning the tactical battle is slow and manual.

## What ShapeShift does
ShapeShift turns synthetic football events into explainable match intelligence in four steps:

1. **Shape detection:** Infers each team's shape in possession and out of possession (for example a back four that builds into a 3 2 5).
2. **Overload analysis:** Measures numerical advantages by zone (wide, half spaces, central) and links them to xG for and against, across a full synthetic season.
3. **Live prediction:** Updates every minute with the current shape and overloads to estimate next goal probability, expected xG for the next 15 minutes and counter attack risk.
4. **Narrative agent:** Writes studio ready storylines such as "Team B moved to a back three and is now overloading the left, raising their chance of scoring next to 34%."

## Explainability
Every insight links back to the exact events, zones and matches behind it. Sample sizes and confidence levels are shown, and early match predictions are labelled low confidence. The narrative agent only describes numbers computed in code, so it cannot invent facts.

## Architecture (Azure)
Synthetic event generator, storage and database for events and shape metrics, analysis and prediction services, a grounded narrative agent on Azure AI Foundry, and a web dashboard with a pitch view, season timeline and "why this changed" panel.

## Data
All data is synthetic. Clubs, players and matches are fictional.

## Goals
Give broadcasters a faster, trustworthy way to explain tactics, and give viewers the story behind the score.

title: Shield: Play Like Your Idol
tagline: Football's best work often never makes the highlights. Shield turns synthetic match events into explainable stories, showing the attacks a player stopped, not just the goals he scored, then coaches young players to play like them.
description:
## The problem

Highlights show goals and assists. They miss the defensive midfielder who closes passing lanes and ends attacks before they start. Fans never see that work, and kids who want to play like him have nothing to copy.

## What we built

Shield turns a synthetic match into stories a pundit would be happy to read out, proves every sentence against the data, and turns the best player's game into a training plan a 10-year-old can follow.

**Live demo (running on Azure):** https://shield.prouddune-3a546552.uksouth.azurecontainerapps.io
**Code:** https://github.com/digitaladaption/shield (public, MIT, one-script Azure deploy)
**Demo video (1:58):** https://youtu.be/0PiN3IwhG2c

Five stages: ingest, interpret, explain, render, personalize.

1. **Synthetic data generator.** A seeded simulator produces passes, shots, tackles, interceptions, pressure events and every player's position twice a second. It plants a known "Shield" archetype so the engine can be graded, and a control run with him switched off shows what he was worth. No real Premier League data is used.
2. **Deterministic stats engine.** Danger per moment, possession sequences, momentum, control versus chaos, pass difficulty, sprint speed, player fingerprints and archetypes. Every fact carries event IDs. No model touches a number.
3. **Threat prevented.** Our headline metric credits a player with the danger an attack was heading towards when he stopped it. Goals and assists record what happened; this records what did not. An empirical "without him" counterfactual is built from the match's own possessions.
4. **Verified narration.** Three agents on Microsoft Agent Framework with a Microsoft Foundry model: a Narrator writes from the fact packet and must cite fact IDs; a Verifier (plain code, cannot be talked round) rejects any sentence whose numbers or names are not in the cited facts and sends it back; a Personalizer re-tells the verified story as a native pundit in the viewer's language. Every story carries its full agent trace, so you can watch a draft get rejected and rewritten.
5. **What he sees.** Click any player at any moment: every passing lane open, contested or blocked, the goal wedge, tackle range, who he is marking, computed with the simulator's own geometry.

## Play like your idol

For coaches and 9 to 14 year olds. Pick a way of playing (The Shield, The Metronome, The Creator) and the playbook shows what it looks like, where he stands, what he does first when he wins the ball, his main points from today's match (every one clickable onto the pitch replay), what he is best at and what to work on. A fourth agent, the Coach, turns that into a four-week plan for the child's age band, checked by its own Plan Verifier against a drill library. Enter a kid's simple stats and it finds the archetype whose shape they resemble. Style, not level.

## The voice

Stories are written in the register of a studio pundit: judgement first, the number as proof, yards and the six-yard box rather than metres, the 40th minute rather than 39:40. The Verifier enforces it: exclamation marks, em dashes and the words AI reaches for (showcase, testament, masterclass, pivotal) are rejected whether they came from a template or the model. English, Spanish, German and French.

## Real time

A server-sent event feed replays the match at any speed; an incremental tracker flags key moments with its own measured latency and pushes verified captions. The pipeline is event-driven, so a real feed is an adapter, not a redesign.

## Microsoft technologies

- **Microsoft Agent Framework**: four agents (Narrator, Verifier, Personalizer, Coach) in two WorkflowBuilder graphs, each with a conditional reject-and-rewrite loop
- **Microsoft Foundry**: the model behind the Narrator, Personalizer and Coach, called through a managed identity
- **MCP**: the stats engine is an MCP server, the agents' only route to the numbers (13 tools)
- **Azure Container Apps** and **Azure Container Registry**: the live demo, built and deployed by one script in the repo
- **GitHub Copilot** during development

## Honest limits

The generator is a possession simulator, not physics; the Shield's interception count is exaggerated so he is detectable. Danger is deliberately simple so it can be explained to a child. Video of children is a safeguarding question first and a computer vision question second, so it is out of scope.

title: Shift11 – AI-Powered Football Momentum Attribution
tagline: Detect the shift. Attribute the player. Explain why the game changed.
description:
Shift11 is an AI-powered football analytics system designed to answer a question that traditional match statistics often fail to explain: when did the game change, who caused the change, and why did it matter? Shift11 processes a synthetic football event stream and uses a deterministic analytics engine to track match state, possession, territory, progressive actions, pressure, recoveries, shots, and momentum. It detects meaningful momentum shifts rather than simply displaying raw statistics.

The core innovation is the Momentum Attribution Engine. When a significant shift occurs, Shift11 identifies the primary and secondary players responsible, assigns contribution scores, classifies their role, and reconstructs the sequence of events that produced the change. For example, a momentum shift may be traced through a recovery → progressive carry → line-breaking pass → shot sequence.

Each detected shift is supported by an evidence chain and before-and-after metrics, making the analysis explainable and verifiable. Microsoft AI technologies are then used to transform these verified analytical facts into grounded tactical explanations rather than allowing AI to invent match events or statistics.

The system is designed to provide different levels of insight for different audiences, from simple match explanations for casual viewers to deeper tactical analysis for football enthusiasts and analysts. Shift11 combines deterministic football analytics, player attribution, evidence-based causal analysis, and Microsoft AI to transform raw match events into an understandable story of how the game changed.

The project is being developed using Python, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Azure, with an interactive interface for visualizing momentum timelines, player contributions, event chains, and tactical insights.

title: SignalFlow

description:
SignalFlow is an AI-powered attention and decision engine for live football broadcasts.  
A live match can generate dozens of meaningful signals at the same time: dangerous attacks, pressure shifts, player milestones, tactical changes, possession swings, and more. SignalFlow does not simply generate more insights. It decides which story deserves the audience's attention now.  
The system ingests synthetic football events, transforms them into evidence-backed candidate insights, evaluates their impact and urgency, remembers what has already been shown, and intelligently chooses whether an insight should be shown now, held, scheduled next, or suppressed.  
SignalFlow also adapts the selected story for different audiences, such as analysts, casual fans, and player-focused viewers.  
The architecture combines deterministic football analytics with specialized AI agents for insight discovery, impact evaluation, attention planning, verification, and audience adaptation.

Windows Test Build: https://github.com/kamal-saleh/SignalFlow/releases/tag/v1.0.0

### Testing Instructions

1. Download and extract the [Windows x64 test build](https://github.com/kamal-saleh/SignalFlow/releases/tag/v1.0.0).
2. Run `SignalFlow.Web.exe`.
3. Open `http://localhost:5000` in a browser.
4. To test AI-generated commentary, install and start Ollama, then download the model using `ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`.
5. Keep Ollama running while using the AI commentary feature.

The project uses synthetic football match data. AI commentary requires Ollama and the `qwen2.5:3b` model on the same machine.

title: Sisyphus Engine
tagline: Sisyphus Engine quantifies the relentless physical strain, velocity decay, and pressing fatigue of teams chasing possession... transforming high-frequency synthetic telemetry into real-time momentum intelligence and multi-agent broadcast commentary.
description:
# Project Title
Sisyphus Engine

# Description

## Overview
High-pressing teams frequently lose control when physical fatigue sets in, but traditional broadcast statistics only show overall distance or possession share long after the shift occurs. Sisyphus Engine is a real-time analytics pipeline that processes synthetic player tracking data to measure physical drop-off as it happens on the pitch. By calculating rolling sprint volume, average movement speed, and team compactness, the engine detects when a team's press is breaking down and generates live, synchronized commentary explaining tactical momentum shifts.

## Problem
Standard match statistics are static and retrospective. Broadcasters and viewers rarely have visibility into physical exhaustion until a defensive error occurs or a goal is conceded. Sisyphus Engine solves this by tracking physical output continuously across rolling windows, giving commentators and fans immediate insight into energy loss and changing match dynamics.

## Key Features
- Live Fatigue Tracking: Calculates rolling 5-minute averages of player speed, sprint frequency, and defensive team compactness (spatial area covered).
- Team Energy Index: Produces a live momentum score that flags significant drops in pressing intensity.
- Multi-Agent Commentary: Uses specialized agents to identify fatigue triggers and generate context-aware match commentary.
- Dual Viewer Views: Delivers tailored visual outputs, including a simple momentum gauge for casual fans and detailed speed and spatial metrics for tactical analysts.

## Pipeline Architecture
1. Ingest: Reads synthetic tracking data and action events from Google Research Football and SPADL streams using kloppy and pandas.
2. Interpret: Runs continuous sliding windows to calculate speed decay, sprint volume, and team pitch coverage.
3. Explain: Detects fatigue breakpoints and triggers language model agents to explain why a team's defensive structure is failing.
4. Render: Formats analytical payloads into timed JSON ready for broadcast graphics overlays.
5. Personalize: Adjusts data depth and commentary tone for casual viewers versus tactical analysts.

## Tech Stack
- AI and Orchestration: Microsoft Foundry, Azure Agent Framework, GitHub Copilot SDK
- Data Processing: Python 3.12, pandas, numpy, scipy, kloppy, SPADL
- Cloud and Infrastructure: Azure Container Apps, Azure Functions
- Frontend: Streamlit dashboard with pitch visualizer and live commentary feed
- Data Source: Google Research Football synthetic tracking feeds

## Target Categories
- Grand Prize: Complete real-time match intelligence pipeline.
- Best Multi-Agent System: Coordinated multi-agent workflow split across telemetry monitoring, tactical analysis, and audience formatting.
- Best Azure Cloud Native Integration: Scalable, containerized streaming backend deployed on Azure Container Apps.

## The problem
Broadcasters pay people to watch every match and tag each pass, shot and tackle by hand. Then a producer decides which stats to show on screen. It is slow, expensive, and the same graphics go to every viewer.

## What Spotter does
1. **Synthetic matches:** our own simulator generates fictional matches with realistic football (event counts match real-football averages) and renders them as broadcast-style video. It also records the true events, so we can measure our accuracy exactly.
2. **Auto-eventing:** a computer vision pipeline watches only the video. It detects players and the ball, tracks them, maps pixels to pitch coordinates, and turns movement into events with speed and distance.
3. **Explainable intelligence:** agents explain why a moment matters. A verifier agent recomputes every number before it can be shown, and every graphic cites the events behind it.
4. **AI director:** picks which graphic to show, waits for a calm moment instead of covering an attack, and personalizes it: analyst or casual mode, favourite club or player, and language.

## Built with
Microsoft Foundry and Agent Framework (explainer, verifier, director agents), Azure services for hosting and streaming, GitHub Copilot, Python, YOLO, Three.js.

## Status
Work in progress. Simulator and shared data formats done; renderer, vision pipeline and agents in progress.

title: Synthetic Match Insights Engine
tagline: A multi-agent AI pipeline and studio UI that turns synthetic football events into explainable match insights, live multilingual narratives, automated recaps and broadcast overlay cues, personalised for each viewer.
description:
THE PROBLEM

Football produces a constant stream of events such as passes, shots, fouls, substitutions and goals. Turning that stream into something a broadcaster or a fan can understand is slow and mostly manual. Analysts have to watch, interpret and write by hand, and the result is rarely personalised. Most tools show what happened. Very few explain why it matters, and almost none do it in the viewer's own language. This project tackles that gap by automating the path from raw events to explainable, personalised match intelligence.

WHAT THE PROJECT DOES

The Synthetic Match Insights Engine is an AI pipeline with a studio-style user interface. It takes a stream of synthetic football events, either generated from a seed or supplied by the user through an API, and turns them into match insights, live narratives, automated recaps and overlay cues for broadcast graphics. Everything is personalised per viewer and available in five languages. All clubs, players and data are fictional, so the project works without any real match data.

HOW THE PIPELINE WORKS

The system is built as six cooperating agents that run one after another, coordinated by a single orchestrator.

The Ingest agent receives the raw events, validates them and puts them in the correct sequence, so the rest of the pipeline can trust its input.

The Interpreter agent works out the state of the match from those events. It computes values such as expected goals (xG) and momentum, which describe how dangerous each team is and which side is on top at any moment.

The Explainer agent ranks the key moments of the match and attaches a reason to each one, along with the evidence behind it. This is what turns a plain list of events into an explanation of why a moment matters.

The Narrator agent writes captions and commentary for the live feed. It produces them in five languages in a single call to a language model.

The Overlay agent converts the key moments into structured JSON cues in a format called overlay.cue/1, which broadcast graphics systems can use to show lower-thirds and on-screen graphics.

The Personalizer agent shapes the final feed for each viewer, for example by their chosen language and by viewing mode such as broadcast mode.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS

Grounded narration. Language models can invent numbers, so the Narrator never trusts the model blindly. The model's text is accepted only if every number in it is supported by the facts the Interpreter computed. If any number is not supported, or if the model fails or runs out of time, the system falls back to a deterministic template caption. This means a model failure or a hallucination can never block the match or put false statistics in front of a viewer.

A single orchestrator. All agents share one pipeline state and pass work to each other through the orchestrator. It handles retries and fallbacks, and it records a trace of every step. That trace is visible in the studio interface under the option "Show agent trace", so a user can see exactly how an insight was produced.

The browser engine matches the backend engine. The frontend contains its own simulator and engine, and the backend contains the same logic. Both produce identical matches and identical insights, and a parity script checks this on four different seeds. As a result, the interface starts playing immediately on its own simulator, and when the backend responds it switches to the backend's agent output. This also hides the delay caused by the free hosting service waking up after being idle.

Provider-agnostic configuration. The language model provider can be set to template (no keys needed), GitHub Models, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or Azure. Storage can be set to memory, SQL or Cosmos DB. These are changed through environment variables, so moving between local use, free hosting and Azure needs configuration changes rather than code changes. Spend guards limit which seeds may call the language model and how many calls are made per match, which keeps costs under control.

INTERFACES

The backend exposes a REST and streaming API. The match endpoint returns the full bundle for a given seed. The feed endpoint returns the personalised feed. The overlay endpoint returns broadcast cues. The stream endpoint replays a match live using server-sent events. A custom match endpoint accepts a POST request so users can bring their own events. There are also endpoints for viewer profiles, configuration and health checks.

FRONTEND

The interface is built with React and Vite. It uses GSAP and ScrollTrigger for animation, including a pinned walkthrough of the pipeline, reveal effects and lower-third graphics. Lenis provides smooth scrolling and is kept in sync with GSAP. The visual components come from React Bits, including effects such as Aurora, SplitText, GradientText, ShinyText, ScrollReveal, SpotlightCard, BorderGlow, GlareHover, ElectricBorder, Magnet and ClickSpark.

TECHNOLOGY AND HOSTING

The backend is written in Python with FastAPI. It has 26 automated tests covering the simulator, the engine, the agents, the grounding check, retries, the language model time budget, startup warm-up, providers, storage, the API, streaming and CORS. The project is designed to run entirely on free services, using Neon for the Postgres database, Render for the backend, Vercel for the frontend and GitHub Models for the optional language model. Adapters for Azure OpenAI or Foundry and for Cosmos DB are included behind configuration, so the project can move to Azure.

PROJECT GOALS

The main goal is to show that match intelligence can be explainable, trustworthy and personalised at the same time. Every claim the system makes should be traceable back to computed evidence, and the system should keep working even when the language model fails. A secondary goal is to give broadcasters ready-to-use overlay data and give fans commentary in the language they prefer.

CURRENT LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

The orchestrator is a small implementation written for this project, and it is not built on Microsoft Agent Framework. The Azure adapters exist but have not yet been deployed or tested against a real Azure account. The system does not detect events automatically from video, and it follows one focus player at a time rather than a multi-player watchlist. The next steps are to move the orchestration to Microsoft Agent Framework, deploy on Azure, and add multi-player watchlists.

title: Tactical SuperIntelligence
tagline: Change the Lens. Rethink the Game.
description:
Tactical SuperIntelligence is an interactive second-screen platform that helps everyday football fans understand matches in real time by “changing the lens” and viewing the same game moment through multiple managerial philosophies. Today, fans can see what happens, but most explanations are locked into a single perspective; our concept lets fans compare tactical worldviews side-by-side to learn faster and stay more engaged during live play.

For the hackathon MVP, the experience is **problem-first**: we’ll use a **simulated/manual real-time game state** (key events plus a simplified pitch/shape representation) to prove the core interaction without relying on hard-to-integrate live tracking feeds. As the match state updates, the platform explains what each lens “notices,” why it interprets the situation that way, and what decision it would recommend next.

The MVP will include at least two contrasting tactical lenses:
- **High press / gegenpress lens** vs **mid-block / containment lens** (e.g., “press the center back now to force a turnover” vs “drop into a compact block to protect central lanes and delay”)
- **Possession / positional play lens** vs **direct / transition lens** (e.g., “recycle and create an overload to progress safely” vs “play early into the channel to exploit space before the defense sets”)

**Expected impact:** fans become more tactically fluent and engaged by receiving timely, explainable prompts (“what to watch next” and “why this choice fits this philosophy”), while also learning the tradeoffs between different managerial approaches instead of assuming there is one “correct” way to play.

Ultimately, I want TacticLens to make football analytics more accessible and interesting, while ensuring that the explanations it gives are supported by the data.

title: TactiPulse SI
tagline: Super Intelligence for Football. An AI-powered tactical analyst that transforms synthetic match events into explainable tactical insights, detects game-changing patterns in real time, and delivers personalized intelligence for fans, analysts, and broadcasters.
description:
# TactiPulse SI — Super Intelligence for Football Tactical Analysis

**Beyond the scoreline. Beyond statistics. Understand the intelligence behind every match.**

## Overview

**TactiPulse SI (Super Intelligence)** is an AI-powered football tactical intelligence platform designed to transform synthetic, football-realistic match events into real-time tactical insights, explainable narratives, and personalized analytical experiences.

As an individual developer passionate about football, data engineering, and artificial intelligence, I am building TactiPulse SI to explore how advanced AI technologies can make complex football tactical analysis more accessible, interactive, and understandable.

Football is much more than goals, possession percentages, and individual statistics. Every pass, tackle, interception, pressing action, and transition contributes to the tactical story of a match. However, identifying meaningful patterns and understanding their impact often requires specialized knowledge and extensive manual analysis.

TactiPulse SI addresses this challenge by introducing an **AI Tactical Analyst** capable of continuously interpreting match events, detecting meaningful tactical patterns, identifying changes in match dynamics, and explaining the evidence behind those changes.

## The Problem

Traditional football analytics platforms primarily focus on descriptive statistics that explain **what happened** during a match.

However, statistics alone rarely explain:

- Why one team is gaining tactical control over another.
- How pressing intensity influences possession and attacking opportunities.
- When a tactical adjustment changes the momentum of a match.
- Which players contribute most significantly to attacking progression.
- Where defensive vulnerabilities are emerging.
- How individual events connect to broader tactical patterns.

My goal is to move beyond descriptive analytics and develop an intelligent system capable of explaining **what is happening, why it matters, and how the game is evolving**.

## The Solution

At the core of TactiPulse SI is the **Tactical Turning Point Detector**, an analytical engine designed to identify significant tactical changes as a match unfolds.

By continuously processing synthetic football events, the platform will calculate tactical indicators and identify meaningful patterns across several analytical dimensions.

### Key Capabilities

**1. Real-Time Tactical Intelligence**

Analyze incoming passes, shots, tackles, interceptions, recoveries, possession changes, and pressure events to generate meaningful tactical indicators.

**2. Tactical Momentum Detection**

Identify changes in territorial dominance, attacking progression, match rhythm, and defensive pressure through rolling-window analysis and tactical change detection.

**3. Pressing and Defensive Intelligence**

Analyze pressing intensity, high recoveries, defensive interventions, and opposition build-up disruption to identify changes in defensive behavior.

**4. Passing and Possession Intelligence**

Evaluate passing accuracy, progressive passes, possession sequences, passing combinations, and player involvement to identify attacking patterns and tactical dependencies.

**5. Tactical Turning Point Detection**

Automatically identify significant changes in match behavior and explain the statistical evidence supporting each tactical interpretation.

**6. Explainable AI Insights**

Generate contextual explanations supported by tactical metrics, match timestamps, and underlying synthetic events, making every major insight transparent and verifiable.

## Agentic AI Architecture

TactiPulse SI will leverage **Microsoft Foundry** and **Microsoft Agent Framework** to develop an intelligent, multi-agent analytical workflow.

The proposed architecture includes specialized agents with clearly defined responsibilities:

- **Tactical Analyst Agent:** Interprets structured football statistics, evaluates tactical patterns, and produces contextual tactical assessments.
- **Narrative Intelligence Agent:** Transforms analytical findings into natural-language explanations, match narratives, and automated recaps.
- **Evidence Verification Agent:** Validates generated tactical explanations against calculated statistics and supporting match events.
- **Personalization Agent:** Adapts tactical insights to different audiences, preferred languages, favorite teams, and individual players.

The system will combine deterministic statistical calculations with generative AI to produce reliable, contextual, and evidence-grounded tactical intelligence.

## End-to-End Match Intelligence Pipeline

The solution will implement the five-stage pipeline required by the challenge:

1. **Ingest:** Stream synthetic, football-realistic match events through an event-driven data pipeline.
2. **Interpret:** Transform raw events into tactical metrics, possession patterns, pressing indicators, and match-state intelligence.
3. **Explain:** Use AI agents to interpret relevant tactical changes and generate evidence-based explanations.
4. **Render:** Present tactical intelligence through interactive pitch visualizations, dashboards, match timelines, and structured broadcast overlays.
5. **Personalize:** Deliver different analytical experiences according to audience preferences, football knowledge, favorite teams, players, and language.

## Personalized Experiences

TactiPulse SI is designed to support three complementary experiences.

### Tactical Analyst Mode

An advanced analytical environment featuring:

- Tactical momentum indicators.
- Pressing and territorial control analysis.
- Passing networks and progressive passing statistics.
- Player contribution analysis.
- Interactive tactical timelines.
- AI-generated explanations supported by match evidence.

### Fan Mode

An accessible experience focused on:

- Simple explanations of complex tactical concepts.
- Favorite-team and player-focused insights.
- Automatically detected key moments.
- Personalized match narratives.
- Natural-language interaction with the AI Tactical Analyst.

### Broadcast Studio Mode

A production-oriented experience providing:

- Real-time tactical insights.
- Automated tactical commentary.
- Contextual match narratives.
- Timestamped and machine-readable graphical overlays.
- Multilingual storytelling.
- Automated halftime and full-time tactical recaps.

## Microsoft and Azure Technology Stack

The proposed solution will leverage the following technologies:

| Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Foundry | AI models, agent development, evaluation, and observability |
| Microsoft Agent Framework | Multi-agent orchestration and specialized analytical workflows |
| Azure Event Hubs | Real-time synthetic football event ingestion |
| Azure Functions | Event-driven processing and tactical metric computation |
| Azure Container Apps | Cloud-native deployment and application hosting |
| Azure Storage | Synthetic match datasets, event history, and analytical outputs |
| Python | Tactical analytics, statistical modeling, and pattern detection |
| FastAPI | Backend APIs and tactical intelligence services |
| React and TypeScript | Interactive dashboard and real-time tactical visualizations |

## Innovation

The main innovation behind TactiPulse SI is its ability to connect **real-time tactical pattern detection with explainable, personalized AI storytelling**.

Rather than generating isolated statistics or generic commentary, the system will identify meaningful tactical developments, connect them to supporting evidence, and communicate their significance to different audiences.

The Tactical Turning Point Detector will serve as the foundation of this approach, enabling the platform to recognize important changes in match behavior and translate them into contextual intelligence.

A key design principle is that **AI explanations must be grounded in calculated statistics and identifiable match events**, ensuring transparency and reducing unsupported interpretations.

## Expected Impact

TactiPulse SI aims to demonstrate how artificial intelligence can transform football analytics into accessible, responsive, and engaging intelligence.

Potential applications include:

- **Football Analysts:** Accelerating tactical analysis and identifying meaningful patterns.
- **Broadcasters:** Automating contextual commentary and tactical storytelling.
- **Streaming Platforms:** Enabling personalized and interactive viewing experiences.
- **Football Fans:** Making advanced tactical concepts easier to understand.
- **Developers:** Providing an extensible foundation for future AI-powered sports analytics solutions.

## Synthetic Data and Responsible AI

The platform will exclusively use **synthetic, football-realistic datasets**, including generated players, teams, match events, and tactical scenarios.

No real Premier League match data will be redistributed or required.

The project will prioritize explainability, statistical consistency, reproducibility, and responsible AI practices throughout the analytical pipeline.

## Vision

My vision is to develop an intelligent football analysis platform that bridges the gap between complex tactical data and meaningful football understanding.

By combining data engineering, real-time analytics, specialized AI agents, and interactive visualization, TactiPulse SI aims to make every tactical development understandable and every match more engaging.

**TactiPulse SI — Don't just watch the game. Understand the game.**

tagline: From match events to meaningful stories: real-time AI that explains what happened, why it matters, and who it matters to.
description:
Tactiq is a real-time, agentic football intelligence engine that turns live match events into insights fans can actually understand.

Instead of simply reporting statistics such as possession, passes, shots, or tackles, Tactiq analyzes how those events combine to reveal changes in pressure, momentum, rhythm, and player influence. It then uses Microsoft Foundry agents to explain those insights in a way that matches the viewer.

The system runs on a reproducible synthetic football match, allowing the entire experience to be demonstrated without relying on proprietary Premier League data or copyrighted match footage.

How it works

Tactiq follows a simple principle:

Events produce facts. Facts produce patterns. Agents explain patterns.

The system:

Generates a realistic synthetic football match and streams events in real time.
Converts events into deterministic football metrics and match state.
Detects meaningful patterns such as sustained pressure, momentum/rhythm shifts, and player influence.
Attaches evidence and time windows to every insight.
Uses Microsoft Foundry agents to explain the insight without inventing match facts.
Personalizes the explanation for casual fans, analysts, or a selected player.
Localizes the validated insight into different languages, with Kiswahili as a core demonstration language.
Converts localized commentary into speech for the demonstrated language path.
Produces a grounded post-match recap from the insights generated during the match.
Why it matters

Football generates enormous amounts of event data, but raw statistics do not always explain the story of a match.

A viewer might see that a team has completed more passes or increased possession, but what they really want to know is:

What is changing? Why does it matter?
Tactiq is designed to bridge that gap by transforming raw match events into evidence-backed explanations that can adapt to different audiences.

A casual fan can receive a short, simple explanation. An analyst can receive deeper tactical context and supporting metrics. A player-focused view can highlight only evidence-supported contributions from the selected player.

Built for the challenge

The project uses synthetic, football-realistic data and is designed around the challenge pipeline:

Ingest → Interpret → Explain → Render → Personalize

The architecture separates deterministic football intelligence from generative AI. This means AI agents are responsible for explaining and presenting verified football facts rather than creating statistics or match events.

The project is being built with Microsoft technologies including Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI services, Azure hosting, and agentic workflows, alongside Python/FastAPI and a TypeScript web experience.

Vision

Tactiq aims to make football intelligence feel less like a statistics dashboard and more like having an intelligent analyst sitting beside you, explaining the story of the match as it unfolds.

Current focus: a reliable end-to-end experience covering synthetic live match simulation, evidence-backed insights, agentic explanation, personalization, Multilangual localization, spoken commentary, and grounded post-match recap.

Future direction: broader language support, additional football patterns, richer broadcast-compatible outputs, and deeper cloud-native infrastructure.

Project principle: AI should explain the game, not make up the game.

title: TactIQ
tagline: Transforming synthetic match data into explainable tactical intelligence for modern broadcasting.
description:
TactIQ: Agentic Match Intelligence for Premier League Studio

Overview

Football stories do not start and end with the scoreline. TactIQ is a full-stack, AI-driven match intelligence platform built on Microsoft Azure that transforms synthetic Premier League event data into deep, explainable tactical insights. Designed specifically for studio broadcasters, analysts, and fans, the platform goes beyond raw numbers by programmatically answering why a moment mattered during a match.

How It Works: The 5-Stage Pipeline & Task Decomposition
TactIQ implements a robust Agentic AI Workflow using Azure OpenAI (GPT-4o) via Microsoft Foundry. When raw synthetic match data (passes, shots, pressures, and player tracking) streams into the application, our proprietary Task-Decomposition Algorithm breaks complex queries down into four sequential processing steps:

Filter: Programmatically isolates relevant events, time windows, and players from Microsoft's official dataset.

Compute: Calculates micro-statistics such as pass difficulty ratings, pressure intensity, and player speed thresholds.

tagline: No evidence, no airtime. The Gallery transforms live football event streams into verified, explainable, producer-ready coverage. Every insight is linked to evidence, fact-checked before approval, and automatically adapted for different broadcast markets and languages.
description:
# The Gallery

**No evidence, no airtime.**

The Gallery is an AI-powered producer's assistant for live football broadcasts. It sits between a live match event feed and the production team, transforming football events into trusted, evidence-backed editorial packages that broadcasters can confidently approve and put on air.

Today's AI tools can generate match stories in seconds, but speed alone is not enough for live television. Every statistic, headline and insight must be accurate, explainable and auditable. One unsupported claim on air becomes a public mistake.

The Gallery addresses this by combining deterministic analytics with Microsoft AI. Rather than allowing an LLM to invent statistics or interpret raw match data, every insight is first detected using deterministic algorithms. The AI receives only verified evidence and generates natural-language storylines that are checked again before reaching a producer.

Our core principle is:

> **Numbers come from code. Words come from AI. Every word must point back to a number.**

The system continuously:

- Detects important tactical moments and match turning points.
- Scores and ranks the stories most worthy of broadcast.
- Generates structured editorial content.
- Verifies every factual claim against the underlying event data.
- Allows producers to approve, edit or reject stories with a complete audit trail.
- Adapts coverage for different markets and languages rather than simply translating text.
- Produces ready-to-use halftime and full-time broadcast packages.

A built-in benchmark evaluates both detector performance and AI reliability by replaying synthetic football matches containing known tactical patterns and intentionally injected false claims. The Gallery measures how quickly meaningful stories are produced while ensuring unsupported claims never reach the producer.

The project is built using Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure Container Apps, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, Microsoft Fabric, Azure AI Search and Azure Static Web Apps.

The Gallery demonstrates how trustworthy, explainable AI can become an editorial partner for broadcasters rather than simply another text-generation tool.

title: The Gallery — An AI Broadcast Crew for Every Fan
tagline: A team of AI agents that watches every pass, explains why moments matter, and produces a personalised, fact-checked broadcast for every fan, in their language.
description:
## The problem
Football stories don't start and end with the scoreline. Broadcasters and streaming platforms produce one feed for millions of fans, and that one feed serves nobody fully. The casual viewer drowns in jargon, the analyst wants more depth, and a fan in Mumbai or Madrid wants it in their own language. Existing stat graphics report *what* happened, but rarely explain *why it matters*.

## What we're building
**The Gallery** is an AI broadcast crew: a team of specialised agents modelled on a real TV production gallery. It watches every event of a match in real time, works out what matters, explains why, and produces a personalised, fact-checked broadcast for every viewer.

## How it works: one pipeline, five stages
1. **Ingest:** Our own synthetic match simulator streams football-realistic events (passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, pressure events, player positions) in real time. Teams carry tactical profiles (high press, low block, tactical switches), so the data contains ground truth we can measure our insights against.
2. **Interpret:** A deterministic stats engine computes player speed and distance tags, pass quality (distance, accuracy, difficulty rating), ball and shot speed, and three signature meters: **Control vs Chaos**, **Pressure**, and **Game Rhythm**.
3. **Explain:** A multi-agent crew (Match Director, Tactical Analyst, Moment Judge, Storyteller, Fact-Checker, Fan Producer) works over shared match state via an MCP server. It explains why moments matter. Every claim is verified against the numbers before it reaches the screen.
4. **Render:** Insights are emitted as timed, machine-readable overlay events, ready for a graphics partner, and shown live on a 2D match view. Every overlay has a "Why?" button that shows the evidence.
5. **Personalise:** The same match becomes genuinely different experiences: Casual Fan mode (with a Jargon Decoder), Analyst mode, favourite club, Player Cam, single-metric focus, and multilingual text and spoken recaps.

## Built with
Microsoft Foundry (Agent Service, evaluations), Microsoft Agent Framework, MCP, Azure OpenAI, Azure Event Hubs, Azure Functions / Container Apps, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SignalR, Azure AI Speech, Azure AI Translator, Azure AI Content Safety, Application Insights, GitHub Copilot.

## Goals
- Explainable: no insight without evidence.
- Real-time enough for live play.
- Production-minded: tracing, evaluations, safety, and graceful fallbacks when a model fails.
- Made for every fan, in every market.

*All clubs, players and match data are fictional and synthetic.*

title: THE HALF-TIME LAB
tagline: Watch the first half. Coach the second.
description:
## THE HALF-TIME LAB

**You’ve watched the first half. Now coach the second.**

THE HALF-TIME LAB transforms half-time from a passive break into an interactive football experience where fans can diagnose the match, make tactical decisions, simulate their plan and forecast what the coach will do.

Most football AI experiences tell fans **what happened**. THE HALF-TIME LAB asks:

**What did you see? What would you change? And can you predict what happens next?**

### How it works

At half-time, AI analyses the first half and identifies the most important tactical problems — such as pressing traps, poor central progression, defensive-line vulnerabilities, isolated players, overloads and dangerous transition situations.

The fan then enters **Coach Mode**.

They can:

* Choose a different formation.
* Make a tactical substitution.
* Adjust pressing intensity.
* Change the build-up approach.
* Choose where to attack.
* Adjust the team's risk level.

The fan then selects **Simulate My Plan**.

A counterfactual tactical model estimates the potential consequences of their decisions, showing trade-offs such as increased chance creation versus greater transition risk.

The simulation is explicitly presented as a modelled counterfactual, not as a claim about what would definitely have happened.

### Predict the Coach

THE HALF-TIME LAB then asks:

**What do you think the coach will do?**

Fans can forecast a substitution, formation change or tactical adjustment, as well as how the team will behave in the second half.

Each synthetic team has a coach profile with characteristics such as risk tolerance, substitution tendencies, formation preferences and responses to the scoreline.

This provides measurable synthetic ground truth.

When the second half begins, the system reveals what the synthetic coach actually did and how the team actually behaved.

### Who read the game?

After the match, THE HALF-TIME LAB compares:

**Your plan**
vs.
**AI recommendation**
vs.
**Your coach forecast**
vs.
**Actual outcome**

The system explains what the fan got right, what they missed and why.

Fans receive a personalised **Football IQ profile**, measuring areas such as tactical recognition, spatial awareness, press recognition, substitution reading, risk assessment and transition reading.

Future challenges can adapt to the fan's strengths and weaknesses.

### Agentic AI

THE HALF-TIME LAB uses specialised agents:

* **Match Diagnosis Agent** — identifies important tactical problems from the match state.
* **Fan Challenge Agent** — decides which tactical question to present to the fan.
* **Tactical Planning Agent** — converts fan choices into a coherent tactical plan.
* **Counterfactual Simulation Agent** — estimates the consequences and trade-offs of that plan.
* **Coach Forecast Agent** — predicts the synthetic coach's likely decisions and second-half behaviour.
* **Outcome & Learning Agent** — compares predictions with reality, explains the result and updates the fan profile.

### Synthetic Football Data

The project uses synthetic, football-realistic data throughout the experience.

A synthetic match generator creates controlled football scenarios including pressing traps, attacking overloads, defensive transitions, defensive-line vulnerabilities and tactical changes.

Because the simulator controls the match environment and coach behaviour, the project has measurable ground truth for evaluating predictions while avoiding redistribution of real Premier League match data.

### Microsoft Technology

The planned architecture uses Microsoft technologies including Microsoft Foundry for agent orchestration, Azure Event Hubs for event streaming, Azure Functions or Container Apps for processing, Azure data services for match state, Microsoft Fabric for analytics, React/TypeScript for the interactive experience and Python for the synthetic football simulator and tactical state engine.

### Vision

THE HALF-TIME LAB is designed as a new live broadcast and second-screen format.

A casual fan can simply watch.

A curious fan can answer tactical questions.

A hardcore fan can become the coach, simulate a plan and forecast the manager.

The goal is not to replace the football expert or tell fans what to think.

**The goal is to make fans better at reading the game.**

**Watch. Diagnose. Coach. Forecast. Learn.**

title: The Metronome: Tactical Turning Point Engine
tagline: An AI-ready match intelligence layer that detects when a football match changes shape, explains the evidence, and translates the moment for analysts, broadcasters, and fans.
description:
## The problem

Football coverage often reports what happened without explaining when the match truly changed shape. Possession, passes, shots, and pressure events become useful only when they are connected into a meaningful football story.

## What we are building

The Metronome: Tactical Turning Point Engine transforms synthetic football events into explainable, real-time match intelligence.

It detects moments such as:

- a press beginning to collapse;
- a team discovering a new progression route;
- territorial control shifting;
- possession becoming less effective;
- transition exposure increasing.

The product does not simply say what happened. It explains why the moment matters and identifies the evidence supporting the conclusion.

## How it works

The pipeline:

1. Ingests synthetic football events such as passes, shots, tackles, pressure events, turnovers, and possession changes.
2. Interprets those events through rolling football metrics.
3. Detects meaningful tactical state changes.
4. Explains the change using evidence from the event stream.
5. Renders the insight for different audiences.

## User experiences

### Analyst Mode

Provides tactical evidence, rolling metrics, affected zones, player involvement, confidence, and source events.

### Broadcast Mode

Generates concise, timed insights suitable for on-screen match coverage.

### Fan Mode

Translates the same intelligence into a clear and accessible explanation for supporters.

## Current MVP

The first MVP includes a deterministic synthetic match engine, a Game Control Index, progressive-exit analysis, pressure effectiveness, a live 2D pitch, event stream, turning-point detection, and Analyst, Broadcast, and Fan modes.

The evidence layer is deliberately deterministic so that AI explains verified football signals rather than inventing conclusions.

## Microsoft technology direction

The project is being developed for Microsoft Foundry and Azure AI integration. Microsoft Foundry will support evidence-grounded narrative generation, audience-specific explanations, and future agent orchestration while the deterministic analytics engine remains the source of truth.

## Why it matters

The same intelligence can support football analysts, broadcasters, streaming platforms, clubs, and supporters. The long-term goal is to make every match more understandable by revealing the tactical story beneath the scoreline.

title: The Ninety Labs
tagline: The Beautiful Game doesn’t stop at what you can see.
description:
Football's event data is still typed by hand. Opta assigns three analysts to every match. StatsBomb uses two per match and delivers within 12 hours. Contract taggers in Manila, Cairo and Chennai are paid around $70 a match to log up to 3,000 actions (Rest of World, 2026). Humans also disagree: at the 2018 World Cup, providers' shot locations differed by more than five yards on 30% of shots. That cost is why data stops at the top flight, and lower leagues, the women's game and academies get none. Downstream, every viewer gets the same overlays. Blind and low-vision fans, over 2M people in the UK alone, depend on human describers available in only some stadiums.

Spotter starts from video rather than from a pre-made event feed.

- Synthetic broadcast. 

A seeded match engine renders broadcast-style footage (camera pans, zoom, occlusion, blur) and keeps a hidden log of every event and position as the answer key.

- Auto-eventing. 

A vision pipeline detects players and the ball, maps the camera view onto the pitch, tracks every player, and derives passes, shots, tackles, possession changes, ball speed, shot speed and sprint speed. 

- Graded in public. 

Spotter scores itself live against the answer key: precision and recall per event, speed error. It publishes a seeded benchmark anyone can rerun.

- Self-improving data. 

When vision struggles, a data agent generates footage aimed at that weakness (crowded boxes, fast pans, blur), and Spotter measures again.

- Explained by agents. 

On Microsoft Agent Framework, an Analyst, a Tactician and a Verifier turn events into explanations of why moments matter, such as control vs chaos and pressure shifts. A Producer decides what airs. Code computes every number, and the Verifier rejects any claim the evidence doesn't support.

- Drawn on the footage. 

Name tags, speeds and pass-difficulty arcs sit on the real video at the detected positions, as timed cues a graphics system can consume.

- Personalized and accessible. 

Analyst or casual view, favorite club, player-focus mode, multilingual commentary, and live audio description for blind and low-vision fans. Every spoken line is built from what the detector saw and traceable to the frames behind it.

tagline: A multi-agent system that turns live football events into explained, verified on-screen overlays, personalized for each viewer by role, club, player and language.
description:
## The problem
A score alert says what happened, not why. Fans get "GOAL 1–0", broadcasters can't produce explained graphics for every market and language, and most of the story behind a match never reaches the people watching.

## What Touchline does
Touchline is a live match producer made of AI agents. It turns a stream of synthetic football events into explained, timed overlays that sit on screen beside the match, personalized for each viewer.

The same match plays out as two different experiences: an analyst gets full metrics in English, while a casual fan gets plain-language explanations in Pidgin or Yoruba, with a mode that follows one player.

## How it works: one pipeline, five stages
1. **Ingest.** A steerable synthetic match simulator streams passes, shots, tackles, pressure events and possession changes through Azure Event Hubs. Scenarios such as a red card or a late press can be injected to replay a match differently.
2. **Interpret.** A deterministic stats engine computes pass difficulty, ball and shot speed, a pressure index, momentum and game rhythm. It is exposed to the agents through an MCP server. The code produces every number; the AI only explains them.
3. **Explain.** Six agents built with Microsoft Agent Framework on Microsoft Foundry coordinate through shared match state:
   - Moment Detector: decides which moments are worth surfacing
   - Tactical Analyst: explains why each one matters
   - Narrator: writes the on-screen line
   - Localizer: adapts it to each language and tone
   - Verifier: rejects any claim not backed by event IDs
   - Director: sets priority, timing and screen slot
4. **Render.** Overlays are timed, machine-readable JSON pushed over SignalR to a live pitch view, in a format a broadcast graphics engine could consume.
5. **Personalize.** Viewers choose role (analyst or casual fan), club, favourite player, language and the metric they care about. Each gets a personalized recap at full time.

## Reliability
If the Verifier rejects a claim, it goes back to the Narrator to rewrite. If an agent times out, the Director shows a template overlay instead, so the screen is never wrong or empty.

## Built with
Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure Event Hubs, Azure Container Apps, Azure SignalR Service, Azure Cosmos DB, MCP, GitHub Copilot.

All data is synthetic; clubs and players are fictional.

description:
Football coverage mostly tells you what happened. Touchline is about why it happened, and who is asking.

We generate synthetic match events (passes, shots, tackles, pressure, possession changes) and stream them live through a pipeline of agents:

- Stats Engine: turns raw events into numbers like possession, pass accuracy, pass difficulty, shot speed, and a running momentum index. All numbers come from code, never from the model.
- Moments Agent: flags the moments worth talking about, such as momentum swings, pressure spikes, elite passes, and big chances.
- Explainer Agent: explains why each moment matters, using only the stats it is given.
- Narrator Agent: writes short live commentary lines and a full-time recap.
- Personalizer Agent: reshapes everything for the viewer. Analyst mode gets the numbers and the tactical detail. Fan mode gets plain language. Club and Player Focus modes follow your team or one player all match. Output works in several languages.

Every insight is also sent as a timed overlay cue (JSON) that a broadcast graphics system could render on top of a live feed. Our web app shows this on a live pitch view.

If an agent fails or times out, the system falls back to a template built from the match stats, so the feed never stops.

Built with Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Agent Framework, FastAPI, Next.js, and Azure Container Apps. All clubs, players, and matches are fictional.

As a match unfolds, the dashboard updates the score, team and player statistics, timeline, shot map, and Pressure & momentum pitch. It also shows key set pieces—including penalties—and links insights to the match events behind them, so people can check the evidence for themselves.

The project uses a Tactical Analyst and a Storyteller workflow with Microsoft Foundry and read-only MCP tools when configured. The story can be tailored for different audiences, teams, players, and languages. Without Foundry credentials, the app clearly labels its local results as demo output.

The built-in match packs use fictional teams and synthetic data. An API-Football adapter is available for testing with real fixtures. When a provider doesn’t supply player-tracking coordinates, the pitch positions are illustrative estimates rather than tracking data.

title: TransferAssist
tagline: An idea to help scouts make right decisions in transfer market.
description:
TransferAssist helps football club executives and coaching staff make faster, safer transfer decisions during short, high-pressure windows by reducing uncertainty about whether a player will succeed in a new system.

The problem it addresses is that players can perform extremely well in one club but underperform after a high-wage transfer because they don’t fit the new team’s playing style, role expectations, or tactical system. Sporting Directors and Head Coaches often need to decide quickly—with incomplete context—whether to approve a signing, and the cost of a wrong decision is high (wages, fees, squad disruption, lost results).

TransferAssist is a problem-first, AI/data-driven shortlist builder designed for Sporting Directors and Head Coaches. A user enters key constraints and context—team style (e.g., possession vs. direct play, pressing intensity), formation, target role, and budget. The app then outputs a ranked shortlist of candidate players, along with plain-language “fit reasons” and highlighted red-flag risks related to system fit and adaptation. The goal is to align decision-makers quickly around evidence-based options, reduce system-mismatch signings, and improve recruitment ROI—especially when time is limited.

Expected impact: quicker approvals with clearer rationale, fewer costly “doesn’t fit the system” transfers, and a more consistent recruitment process that balances coach needs with executive risk management.

title: Turning Point
tagline: Every moment scored by how much it changed the match, and explained for every kind of fan.
description:
Description
Turning Point is an end-to-end pipeline that turns a live stream of synthetic football events into explainable match intelligence.

Synthetic matches are generated with a continuous-time stochastic simulator (Gillespie-style), where event rates depend on possession, pitch zone, pressure and game state. Each match carries hidden ground truth, so the analytics can be validated, not just displayed.

As events arrive, a live engine tracks score, xG, win probability and pass difficulty. A moment’s importance is defined quantitatively: how much it shifted win probability (impact) and how unlikely it was under the model (surprise). A regime detector flags when the game moves between control and chaos.

Each insight is emitted as timed, machine-readable JSON for broadcast overlays, then rendered by an LLM into narratives tailored to the viewer: data-rich analyst mode or story-first casual mode, favourite club, player focus, and multiple languages. After the final whistle, the same insights produce an automated match recap.

title: VendorIQ
tagline: Normalizing football data across vendor formats, with confidence scores you can trust.
description:
VendorIQ is a 7-agent pipeline that takes a football match feed from any major vendor format (Opta, StatsBomb, or Wyscout), normalizes it into a single Common Data Format (CDF) document, and explains it back out as computed stats and narrative text.

The problem - Clubs, broadcasters, and analysts work with match data from multiple vendors, and every vendor structures that data differently. A system built for Opta’s shape breaks on StatsBomb’s, and neither one matches Wyscout. Normalizing this by hand, or with a single rigid script, falls apart the moment real data arrives messy, incomplete, or in a shape the script did not anticipate.

The approach -  Instead of one monolithic parser, the pipeline splits the work across seven specialized agents, each responsible for one stage: detecting the vendor format, mapping it to the unified schema, normalizing pitch coordinates, resolving player identity across vendors, validating and scoring the result, generating stats and narrative text, and exporting back to any vendor’s shape on demand. A Master Orchestrator wires these together and owns the retry, abort, and graceful degradation logic when a stage fails or the input data is incomplete. And then a summary of key points in the match data is shown.

The goal - To Build something a club could actually put into production, not just a hackathon demo. That means the pipeline never fabricates data it does not have. When input data is missing or corrupted, the system degrades gracefully and reports an honest confidence score instead of guessing. Every fallback path is documented and tested.
