title: Virtual Studio Crew: an AI production crew for explainable, personalized football broadcasts
tagline: Five AI agents on Azure turn live match events into explained, fact-checked broadcast graphics, live commentary, and spoken recaps, personalized for every fan: analyst or casual, their club, their player, or one metric they love, in English, Spanish, or French.
description:
## The problem

Football broadcasts tell every fan the same story, and AI that writes sports copy makes numbers up. Broadcasters can't produce a different show for every viewer, and they can't put unchecked AI text on air.

## What we built

**Virtual Studio Crew** is an AI production crew on Azure. It ingests a live stream of synthetic match events and turns them into explained, fact-checked, personalized graphics, commentary, and recaps for every fan at once.

Five agents, built on **Microsoft Agent Framework**, run as a workflow over every important moment:

- **Stats** freeze the facts the instant the moment happens (pass difficulty, xG, ball and shot speed, PPDA, momentum, and control vs. chaos).
- **The Gaffer** explains *why* the moment matters, citing a fact for every claim.
- **Ref** checks every number against the data, rejects season, record, and certainty claims, and then a reviewer agent judges whether the claims follow. Anything that fails goes back for a rewrite. Nothing unverified reaches air.
- **The gallery** decides what still deserves air and drops stories that arrive after play has moved on.
- **The host** rewrites the verified story for each viewer in their language. Ref re-checks every version.

## Made for every fan

- **Personas:** analyst, casual fan, club fan ("we" and "us"), player focus (with a live stat strip and their name on the pitch), and metric focus (follow xG, pass difficulty, pressing, or top speed all match).
- **Three languages:** English, Spanish, and French, each checked by Ref, with decimal commas included.
- **Live commentary:** play-by-play captions in each viewer's language, voiced by **Azure AI Speech** on the big moments.
- **"Why did that happen?":** Any story replays the exact events behind it, then the verified explanation.
- **Spoken full-time recap:** the crew talks you through the match, with a voice for each character.
- **Condensed mode:** a full match in under five minutes, slowing down for the big moments.

## Built for the production path

- Broadcast-style overlays with timing, screen slot, and priority, plus a **versioned overlay timeline (JSON Schema)** for graphics partners.
- The template graphic airs instantly, so the crew never slows the broadcast down.
- Usage limits that degrade gracefully on a public demo and one-command deployment with Bicep.

## Microsoft and Azure technologies

- **Azure AI Foundry** (Azure OpenAI, gpt-4.1-mini), keyless with Microsoft Entra ID and managed identity
- **Microsoft Agent Framework**: agents with sessions and tools, orchestrated as a **workflow** with a review loop
- **Microsoft.Extensions. AI and its evaluation library**: model access, OpenTelemetry, and quality evaluation with Foundry as the judge
- **Azure AI Speech**: neural voices for commentary and recaps
- **Azure Container Apps** and **Azure Container Registry**: hosting and cloud image builds
- **Application Insights**: end-to-end traces of every workflow step, agent run, and model call

## Evidence

- **Evaluation:** on 30 live stories, Ref approves 87% of pitches the first time, and the median time from moment to verified card is 9.9 s. Our first evaluation found Ref rejecting pitches over citation format rather than facts. Fixing that raised first-time approval from 53% to 77% on the same matches.
- **Data:** 100 synthetic matches calibrated to real top-flight figures (2.9 goals per match, 1.4 xG, and 12 shots per team), with a data card documenting the schema and known deviations.
- **Quality:** 92 automated tests and CI on every push.

## Try it

- Live demo: https://studio-crew.politebay-c6735be6.canadacentral.azurecontainerapps.io (pick match 7, press Kick off)
- Code: https://github.com/timmytrace/pl-insights-engine

All clubs, players, and match data are synthetic. Characters designed and modeled by Timilehin Owolabi.

title: VYBE — Every Fan Belongs
tagline: Feel the Game. Your Way. — Human-centered football intelligence that transforms synthetic match events into personalized, accessible, and meaningful experiences for every fan.
description:
# VYBE — Every Fan Belongs

**Feel the Game. Your Way.**

### The Vision

Football brings people together across generations, cultures, languages, and abilities. Yet most digital football experiences present the same statistics, commentary, and analysis to everyone, regardless of their needs or level of understanding.

**VYBE reimagines that experience.**

VYBE is an accessibility-first, Azure-ready football storytelling prototype that transforms synthetic match events into personalized, explainable, and interactive experiences.

Instead of asking every fan to experience football in the same way, VYBE adapts how the story of a match is presented.

**One match. Three perspectives. Every fan belongs.**

### Three Experiences. One Shared Passion.

**1. Young Fan — Learn, Play, Celebrate**

An engaging experience that makes football easier to understand through:

- Interactive goal celebrations and match highlights.
- Simple explanations of football terminology.
- Interactive football quizzes.
- Approachable, event-grounded commentary.

**2. Accessible Fan — Football Without Barriers**

An inclusive experience designed to give fans greater control over how they follow a match:

- English, Arabic, and Czech commentary and captions.
- Optional browser-based spoken commentary with adjustable voice speed.
- High-contrast mode and larger text.
- Keyboard navigation and screen-reader-friendly step-by-step playback.
- Event-synchronized captions and optional descriptions of shots and passes.
- Persistent accessibility preferences within the browser.

These features improve accessibility without claiming complete WCAG certification. Spoken-language quality depends on available browser and operating-system voices.

**3. Analyst Fan — Understand the Game Beyond the Score**

An evidence-grounded analytical experience featuring:

- Match statistics derived from recorded synthetic events.
- Interactive timelines with Highlights, Goals, and All Events filters.
- First-half versus second-half comparisons.
- Interactive 15-minute momentum visualizations.
- Goal turning points and contextual match narratives.

Momentum is calculated from weighted recorded events, rather than presented as possession, expected goals, or professional tactical analysis.

### How VYBE Works

VYBE follows the five-stage workflow of the Synthetic Match Insights Engine challenge.

**Ingest:** Load structured synthetic match events, including goals, shots, and passes.

**Interpret:** Process ordered events through a deterministic engine to calculate match statistics, identify event-activity patterns, and highlight important moments.

**Explain:** Produce persona-specific, evidence-grounded narratives that explain match developments without inventing factual events.

**Render:** Display match intelligence through an interactive React dashboard with replay controls, timelines, captions, and visual insights.

**Personalize:** Adapt the same match to three audiences through different presentation styles, accessibility controls, and user preferences.

A guided demonstration also allows viewers to explore all three experiences using selected match events.

### Technical Architecture and Microsoft Azure

VYBE is built with:

- **React, TypeScript, and Vite** for the interactive frontend.
- **Python and FastAPI** for backend APIs and match processing.
- **A deterministic event engine** for reproducible match facts and statistics.
- **Browser SpeechSynthesis API** for optional spoken commentary.
- **Docker and Azure Container Apps-ready infrastructure** for cloud deployment.
- **Optional Azure AI-assisted narration integration**, with deterministic fallback behavior.

The architecture deliberately separates match facts from presentation and narration.

The core experience operates independently of external AI services, while the backend provides an integration path for Azure-assisted narration.

Microsoft Foundry and more advanced agent orchestration are potential future extensions, not claims of currently deployed capabilities.

### Innovation: Inclusive, Explainable Football Intelligence

VYBE demonstrates that football intelligence should not be limited to professional analysts or technically experienced audiences.

Its innovation is the combination of three principles:

**Accessibility by design:** Fans can adjust language, visual presentation, navigation, and spoken commentary to suit their needs.

**One source of truth, multiple experiences:** The same underlying synthetic events power every persona, reducing inconsistency between different interpretations of the match.

**Explainable insights:** Match narratives and statistics remain grounded in recorded events, with deterministic processing providing a reproducible foundation.

This approach offers a practical prototype for more inclusive sports storytelling across digital fan experiences.

### Engineering Quality and Validation

VYBE has undergone automated and manual validation, including:

- **54/54 backend tests passed.**
- **4/4 Playwright browser tests passed.**
- **24/24 manual end-to-end acceptance checks completed successfully.**
- Successful TypeScript/Vite production and Docker image builds.
- Successful container health endpoint verification.
- GitHub Actions validation.
- Dependency security audits with no known vulnerabilities reported in the audited dependencies.

These results support the reliability of the tested prototype. They do not constitute full production security certification, comprehensive accessibility certification, or completed live Azure validation.

### Responsible Data and AI

VYBE uses a fictional match between Aurora FC and Harbor United.

All teams, players, and match events are synthetic. The prototype does not use official Premier League match feeds or claim real-time match coverage.

Its deterministic event engine remains the source of truth for match facts. Optional AI-assisted storytelling is designed to build on that factual foundation rather than replace it.

### How to Experience VYBE

Explore the three fan experiences through the guided demo or manually switch between Young Fan, Accessible Fan, and Analyst Fan.

Start with Young Fan to experience goal celebrations and interactive learning. Switch to Accessible Fan to explore multilingual captions, spoken commentary, and keyboard-friendly navigation. Finish with Analyst Fan to examine momentum, timelines, and evidence-backed turning points.

The repository provides local setup instructions, architecture documentation, and validation evidence. The hosted demonstration is intended to make the same experiences accessible to judges without local installation once deployed.

### Project Links

**Source Code:** https://github.com/Hapinam/vybe-ai

**Demo Video (53 seconds):** https://youtu.be/c717qul116M

### Our Mission

Football should be understandable, accessible, and engaging for everyone.

VYBE demonstrates how technology can transform one match into multiple meaningful experiences without sacrificing factual grounding.

**VYBE — Feel the Game. Your Way.**

**Every Fan Belongs. Every Moment Matters.**

title: Why That Goal? — See the Play Behind the Finish
tagline: Rewind the goal. Reveal the buildup. Inspect the evidence. A visual match companion that turns synthetic football events into explanations of the decisions and movements behind every finish, tailored to each fan.
description:
## Why That Goal?

**Current stage: in development.** This entry describes the product we are building for Inside the Game. A functioning demo, public repository, measured evaluation and demonstration video will be added before the submission deadline.

### The problem
A goal replay shows the finish. It often hides the recovery, movement and passing decisions that made the finish possible. Fans need a clear visual explanation; analysts and studio producers need to inspect the evidence behind it.

### The experience we are building
Start with the goal, then rewind through its buildup on an animated pitch. Explore the decisive recovery, line-breaking pass and space-creating movement. Select an explanation to jump to its supporting event and see the relevant positions, timing and computed measurements.

The same sequence will support a short, plain-language fan view and a detailed analyst view, with English and Spanish narratives and player focus. A synchronized broadcast overlay and an automatic recap will turn the explanation into something a studio or streaming experience can use.

### One pipeline, five stages
1. **Ingest:** stream original, seeded synthetic match events and fictional player/ball tracking.
2. **Interpret:** calculate match state, distances, passing lanes and pressure indicators in deterministic code.
3. **Explain:** use a focused AI workflow to select the important buildup, query its evidence and write an explanation.
4. **Render:** synchronize pitch annotations, evidence cards and timed overlay instructions with the replay clock.
5. **Personalize:** adapt the verified facts to the viewer's knowledge, chosen player and language.

### Evidence before confidence
The planned evidence pack separates observed events, computed metrics and tactical interpretation. Event citations alone do not prove a tactical claim. Where tracking or context is insufficient, the explanation must say so. Any optional what-if view will be labeled as an illustrative synthetic simulation, never as proof of what would have happened in a real match.

We will evaluate citation validity, numeric consistency, unsupported-claim rejection, explanation quality across audiences/languages, and end-to-end latency on held-out synthetic scenarios. Results and limitations will be published, including failures.

### Microsoft technology plan
Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI will power grounded explanations and evaluation. Azure Container Apps will host the application, with managed identity for service access and Application Insights for operational traces. GitHub will hold the public source and reproducible setup. The final entry will distinguish deployed integrations from planned work.

### Data and scope
All match data, teams and players will be synthetic and fictional. The core experience requires no licensed match feed, real broadcast footage or third-party club branding. This is a football-understanding tool for fans and studios, with a focused goal-buildup experience as its center.

**Goal:** make the play behind the finish understandable, inspectable and useful within one replay.

title: WhyLine
tagline: Not just what happened. Why it mattered, and how we know.
description:
# WhyLine

> **Not just what happened. Why it mattered, and how we know.**

*The match, explained.*

---

## The Problem

Fans are flooded with numbers but starved of meaning:

- **Momentum graphs show who is on top, but never why.**
- **AI-written sports content has a trust problem** after well-publicised factual errors.
- **Streaming delays spoil the action.** Push alerts reveal goals before viewers see them.
- **Personalization is shallow.** It mostly stops at choosing a favourite team.

## What WhyLine Does

WhyLine is a multi-agent match-intelligence system built on **Microsoft Foundry**. It turns a live stream of synthetic football events into explained, verified and personalized storytelling, delivered in sync with each viewer's own stream.

---

## The Pipeline

### 1. Ingest
- A **synthetic match generator** with tactical team profiles (high press, low block, possession) and scripted storylines streams realistic events in real time: passes, shots, tackles, pressure events, possession changes and match metadata.
- **Auto-eventing:** the generator also renders a top-down tracking "video" (player and ball positions per frame). A detector derives passes, ball speed, shot speed and distance covered **from positions alone**, rather than reading them from the event log.

### 2. Interpret
A **deterministic C# stats engine** builds the match state:
- Pass distance, accuracy and **difficulty rating** (distance, pressure on the passer, lines broken)
- Ball and shot speed, distance covered
- Pressing intensity, rhythm and tempo
- **Control-vs-Chaos index** and a **moment-importance score**

### 3. Explain
- **Explained Momentum** annotates every swing in control with its cause and what to watch next.
- A team of agents (below) turns verified facts into narrative.

### 4. Render
- **Timed overlay cues** (player tags, speed and distance badges, insight cards) follow a published JSON schema, ready for a rendering partner.
- **Spoiler-Safe Sync** holds each cue until that viewer's stream reaches the matching match-clock moment.

### 5. Personalize
- **Viewing modes:** Analyst, Casual, Player Focus and Favourite Club.
- **Multi-language commentary** that adapts tone and commentary style, not just words.
- **Catch Me Up** gives late joiners the match so far in seconds, tailored to their club and player.
- **Audio Description** tells blind and low-vision fans where the ball is on the pitch, with spoken output via Azure AI Speech.

---

## Agentic Design: A Virtual Match-Day Newsroom

Code computes every number. Agents decide what matters, write it, check it, and adapt it.

| Agent | Role |
|---|---|
| **Analyst** | Monitors match state, queries the stats engine as a tool, and proposes candidate moments with evidence (event IDs) |
| **Director** | Acts as the producer: decides what goes on screen and when, under a screen-time budget, ranked by moment importance |
| **Narrators** | One per persona (Analyst, Casual, Player Focus, Audio Description); each tells the same moment differently |
| **Localization** | Adapts language, tone and commentary style per market |
| **Verifier** | Checks every claim against the stats engine before release and sends unsupported claims back to the narrator to fix |
| **Recap** | Builds half-time, full-time and Catch Me Up summaries from the verified moment log |

**Orchestration flow:**
`Analyst → Director → Narrators (parallel) → Verifier ⟲ Narrator (on rejection) → Localization → Sync layer`

**Two-speed architecture:**
- **Fast path (milliseconds, code only):** player tags, speed and distance badges, momentum graph.
- **Agent path (seconds):** explanations, narratives, recaps, which is the same latency as a human analyst.

**Agent Trace Panel:** a live view in the UI shows agents proposing, approving, drafting, rejecting and correcting in real time.

---

## Why It Can Be Trusted

- **Numbers come from code; the language model only writes the words.**
- **Every claim has provenance.** Click any sentence and the events behind it light up on the pitch.
- **A Verifier agent** blocks unsupported claims before anyone sees them.
- **Measured, not promised.** Foundry evaluations score groundedness and accuracy across a suite of scripted test matches.

---

## Built on Microsoft Foundry

| Component | Technology |
|---|---|
| Agents & orchestration | **Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET)**, hosted in **Foundry Agent Service**, with multi-agent workflows |
| Stats engine as an agent tool | C# function tools exposed via an **MCP server** |
| Models | Foundry model deployments: a fast model for narrators, a stronger model for Analyst and Verifier |
| Quality | **Foundry evaluations** on groundedness and accuracy |
| Observability | **Application Insights / OpenTelemetry** tracing, which also powers the Agent Trace Panel |
| Speech | **Azure AI Speech** for spoken commentary and audio description |
| App & live delivery | ASP.NET Core, **Blazor**, **SignalR** on Azure Container Apps |

---

## Production Readiness

- **One-command deployment** with `azd up`: Foundry project, model deployments, App Insights, container registry and app.
- **Dockerized** services for local and cloud runs.
- **Tests:**
  - Unit tests for every stats calculation
  - **Golden-match tests:** a scripted match must always produce the expected key moments
  - Verifier regression tests with deliberately false claims
- **Observability dashboard:** latency per agent, Verifier rejection rate and token cost per match.
- **Documented overlay API:** OpenAPI spec plus a JSON schema for the cue format.
- **Resilience:** a cached replay mode keeps the demo running if the network or model quota fails.
- **Architecture diagram and setup guide** in the README.

---

## Hackathon Requirements Coverage

| Requirement | How WhyLine delivers it |
|---|---|
| (i-a) Ingest live synthetic events | Real-time synthetic match generator streaming events |
| (i-b) Interpret into stats and patterns | Deterministic stats engine + Control-vs-Chaos and momentum |
| (i-c) Explain why a moment matters | Explained Momentum + Analyst and Narrator agents |
| (i-d) Render alongside the match | Timed overlay cues with published schema + Spoiler-Safe Sync |
| (i-e) Personalize (club, player, modes) | Analyst / Casual / Player Focus / Favourite Club / Audio Description |
| (ii) Player identification + speed/distance thresholds | Fast-path player tags and threshold-triggered badges |
| (ii) Pass quality | Distance, accuracy and difficulty rating |
| (ii) Ball and shot speed | Computed from tracking data |
| (ii) Auto-eventing | Detector derives events and speeds from positional tracking frames |
| (iii) Narrative generation | Narrator and Recap agents: live narratives, milestones, recaps |
| (iv) Explainability | Control vs Chaos, pressure-wave detection, rhythm + clickable provenance |
| (v) Data innovation | Open synthetic generator with tactical profiles and scripted storylines + sample dataset |
| (vi) Multi-language storytelling | Localization agent with culturally matched commentary styles + Azure AI Speech |

---

## Who It's For
